# Function notes

<!-- generated by `efh notes render` from content/notes/FN-*.json; edits here are overwritten -->

Recorded behaviour of Excel's worksheet functions that an implementation matching Excel needs,
or that explains a result a user did not expect: quirks, answers that differ from the
mathematical value, details of the arithmetic needed to reproduce Excel's last bit, and places
where Microsoft's documentation differs from behaviour. Every note gives exact binary64 inputs
and Excel's recorded answer, the Excel build and machine of the reading, and the evidence. A
note marked measured is read off recorded Excel answers over its stated scope; inferred marks
what goes beyond them. How to add a note: [HOWTO.md](HOWTO.md). Format:
[`tools/schemas/f20-function-note.schema.json`](../../tools/schemas/f20-function-note.schema.json).
Machine-readable: [`site/api/notes.json`](../../site/api/notes.json).

## Summary

- Notes: 329, over 524 functions (of the 554 entries = 531 functions + 23 operators).
- Excel differs from the mathematical answer: 57.
- Detail for matching Excel's bits: 96.
- Quirk: 167.
- Documentation differs from behaviour: 9.
- Measured: 300; inferred: 29.

## Notes

### FN-ABS-001: Text to number checks the exponent range even when the mantissa is zero

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to ABS,
VALUE.

Converting text to a number, measured through ABS and VALUE, rejects a zero mantissa with an
out-of-range exponent: ABS("0e-309") is #VALUE! though the text denotes 0, and ABS("0e-308") is
0. The exponent counts as written, less the fraction digits, less 2 for a percent sign, so
ABS("0.0e309") is 0, ABS("0e309") is #VALUE!, and ABS("0e-307%") is #VALUE!.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=ABS("0e-309")` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel build not recorded in this run; bulk captures of the same date (2026-09-29) record Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2 |
| `=ABS("0e-308")` | as typed | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | — | Excel build not recorded in this run; bulk captures of the same date (2026-09-29) record Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2 |
| `=ABS("0e-307%")` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | — | Excel build not recorded in this run; bulk captures of the same date (2026-09-29) record Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2 |
| `=ABS("0e309")` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel build not recorded in this run; bulk captures of the same date (2026-09-29) record Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2 |

### FN-ABS-002: Subnormal cell writes and *, /, ^ underflows flush to +0, while +, - and EXP(-745) keep subnormals

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-08.* Applies to ABS, CEILING, CEILING.MATH, CEILING.PRECISE,
DELTA, EVEN, EXP, FLOOR, FLOOR.MATH, FLOOR.PRECISE, GESTEP, INT, ISEVEN, ISO.CEILING, ISODD,
ODD, QUOTIENT, SIGN, SQRT.

Writing any positive or negative subnormal binary64 value or -0 to a cell via Range.Value2
stores +0 (0x0000000000000000), while normal extremes 2^-1022 (0x0010000000000000) and ±DBL_MAX
(0x7fefffffffffffff) read back intact. In the 430 recorded bank rows with subnormal or
maximum-finite cell arguments, all 179 subnormal-input rows read back as +0 and match the +0
control (SQRT(-5e-324) is 0, SIGN(±5e-324) is 0, ODD(±5e-324) is 1, EVEN(±5e-324) is 0,
ISEVEN(±5e-324) is TRUE, ISODD(±5e-324) is FALSE, GESTEP(±5e-324) is 1, DELTA(±5e-324) is 1,
and a subnormal divisor or significance in QUOTIENT, CEILING or FLOOR flushes to 0). Formula
literals below 2.2250738585072014E-308 are refused at entry or parsed to 0. Products (*),
quotients (/) and probed powers (^) that fall in the subnormal range flush to +0, whereas + and
- retain subnormals and EXP(-745) holds 0x0000000000000001 in a formula cell. When fed a true
computed subnormal x from EXP(-745), EXP(-730) or EXP(-709) (and 0-x for negative), ABS(±x) is
x, SQRT(+x) is 2^-537, SQRT(-x) is #NUM!, EVEN(±x) is ±2, ODD(±x) is ±1, ISEVEN(±x) is TRUE,
ISODD(±x) is FALSE, CEILING(+x,1) is 1, FLOOR(-x,1) is -1, QUOTIENT(±x,1) is 0, DELTA(x,0) is
0, DELTA(x,x) is 1, GESTEP(+x,0) is 1 and GESTEP(-x,0) is 0, while SIGN(+x) and INT(-x)
transition inside the subnormal range (0 at 0x00000000001c7ea3 and ±1 at 0x0008bfe58468888d).

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SQRT(-5e-324)` | number `-5e-324` (`0x8000000000000001`) (cells) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=EXP(-745)` | as typed | `5e-324` (`0x0000000000000001`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=SQRT(EXP(-745))` | as typed | `2.2227587494850775e-162` (`0x1e60000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=SQRT(0-EXP(-745))` | as typed | `#NUM!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=EVEN(EXP(-745))` | as typed | `2` (`0x4000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=SIGN(EXP(-730))` | as typed | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=SIGN(EXP(-709))` | as typed | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=INT(0-EXP(-730))` | as typed | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=INT(0-EXP(-709))` | as typed | `-1` (`0xbff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20150, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): 430 bank rows replayed with Value2 input read-back and +0 controls, 22
subnormal bit-pattern cell-write probes, 16 literal-acceptance probes, 45 arithmetic underflow
probes, and 180 true-subnormal function calls in Excel 16.0 build 20527 on 2026-11-08.

### FN-ACCRINT-001: ACCRINT uses plain binary64 day-count steps with canonical period normalization and an x87 PC64 final coupon multiply

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20131, 20228, and 20527, ACCRINT(issue, first_interest, settlement, rate,
[par], frequency, [basis], [calc_method]) evaluates day-count fractions in plain binary64
arithmetic normalized by the canonical last coupon period CoupDays(first - 1 period, first)
rather than the settlement period's actual length, sums calc_method=TRUE (default) walks
backward from settlement to issue, skips whole interior coupon periods when calc_method=FALSE
and issue precedes that canonical period, and applies an x87 PC64 multiply followed by binary64
rounding only at the final coupon * accrual product. Matches 146,688/146,688 full-bank and
120/120 pinned ACCRINT rows.

### FN-ACOS-001: ACOS evaluates RN53(RN64(pi/2 - ASIN(x))), inheriting ASIN's 1-ULP sign asymmetry

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ACOS(x) does not satisfy ACOS(-x) = pi - ACOS(x) to the last bit:
ACOS(0.5) returns 0x3ff0c152382d7365 (1.0471975511965976) while ACOS(-0.5) returns
0x4000c152382d7366 (2.0943951023931957), and ACOS(0.75) vs ACOS(-0.75) similarly reflect ASIN's
asymmetric 1 + x = 2 - (1 - x) staging followed by stored x87 subtraction from pi/2. All 13,962
full-bank ACOS rows match this graph.

|---|---|---|---|

| `ACOS(-0.5)` | number `-0.5` (`0xbfe0000000000000`) (cells) | `2.0943951023931957` (`0x4000c152382d7366`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Basis (inferred): Measured across paired signed controls in CalcFunc-Evidence
runs/w111-acos-caller-20260929/answers-acos.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and matched on

### FN-ACOSH-001: ACOSH evaluates LN(x + SQRT(x*x - 1)), returning #NUM! when x*x overflows even where acosh(x) is finite

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ACOSH(x) evaluates LN(x + SQRT(x*x - 1)) via the worksheet LN kernel
rather than a scaled asymptotic branch for large x. When x*x overflows binary64 (above
sqrt(DBL_MAX)), Excel returns #NUM! even though acosh(x) is mathematically finite near 710:
ACOSH(1.7976931348623157e+308) returns #NUM! while ACOSH(1.6449010616608172e+153) returns
353.48634664617043. Under cell Value2 delivery, ACOSH(1 + 2^-52) returns 2.1073424255447014e-08
(0x3e56a09e67ffffff), whereas literal formula entry can round 1+1e-16 down to 1 before
evaluation. All 5,730 full-bank ACOSH rows match.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACOSH(1.7976931348623157e+308)` | number `1.7976931348623157e+308` (`0x7fefffffffffffff`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | `710.475860073944` (`0x408633ce8fb9f87e`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `ACOSH(1.0000000000000002)` | number `1.0000000000000002` (`0x3ff0000000000001`) (cells) | `2.1073424338879928e-08` (`0x3e56a09e67ffffff`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Correct value: ln(2 * DBL_MAX) computed at 120 decimal digits in Python Decimal and rounded to
nearest binary64.

Basis (measured): Measured in Excel 16.0 build 20430 (CalcFunc-Evidence
runs/w111-extended-numeric-20260929/answers/answers-acosh.json.gz) and matched across
5,730/5,730 full-bank ACOSH rows.

Evidence:

- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/src/ported/acosh.rs`, acosh_kernel at `95eb0cb2ef` — LN(x + SQRT(x*x - 1)) implementation and overflow guard
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/witness-status.tsv`, ACOSH at `95eb0cb2ef` — 5,730/5,730 full-bank ACOSH matches
- CalcFunc-Evidence `runs/w111-extended-numeric-20260929/answers/answers-acosh.json.gz`, w111extended-2026092903-ACOSH-00022 at `4ef2c244d7` (readings)

### FN-ACOT-001: ACOT computes ATAN(1/x) with a stored x87 reciprocal, adding pi for negative inputs and returning pi/2 at zero

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

### FN-ACOTH-001: ACOTH switches between a ratio logarithm and an odd-power series at 0x400d92b14ec204f3 and flushes large inputs to +0

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20228, ACOTH computes on |x| and restores the input sign, returning #NUM!
for |x| <= 1 and switching between two x87-staged bodies around |x| = 0x400d92b14ec204f3
(~3.696627): below the switch, 0.5 * LN(RN53(RN64((|x|+1)/(|x|-1)))); at and above it, a
32-term inverse odd-power series sum(1/((2k+1)*|x|^(2k+1))) with every multiply, divide, and
sum stored through x87 PC64. When the initial 1/|x| reciprocal falls below DBL_MIN, both signs
flush to +0 (0x0000000000000000). All 270,010 full-bank ACOTH rows match.

### FN-ADDRESS-001: ADDRESS quotes sheet names resembling R1C1 axis prefixes (even R1048576C16385), omits quotes after [book], and allows signed relative R1C1 offsets

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ADDRESS quotes sheet_text not only for A1 references, spaces,
punctuation, and TRUE/FALSE, but also for any unbracketed name starting with R<1..1048576> or
C<1..16384> or RC<1..16384> not followed by a dot (so R1048576C16385 and R1048576C and R1C000
are quoted, whereas R1048577C16384 is not). A workbook-prefixed sheet_text like [a]TRUE is not
quoted when the book and sheet parts use identifier characters, and empty sheet_text produces
an unquoted '!'. When a1 is FALSE and abs_num selects relative coordinates (abs_num 2, 3, or
4), row_num and column_num admit negative and zero offsets in (-limit+1)..limit and format zero
as R or C without brackets.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ADDRESS(1, 1, 1, TRUE, "R1048576C16385")` | row_num `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); column_num `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); abs_num `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); a1 `TRUE`; sheet_text `R1048576C16385` (cells) | `'R1048576C16385'!$A$1` | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.00), workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

### FN-AMORDEGRC-001: On basis 1, AMORDEGRC and AMORLINC divide actual days by the purchase year's length even across year boundaries

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to AMORDEGRC, AMORLINC.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, when basis is 1 (Actual/Actual) and the first period crosses from a
leap year into a non-leap year (or vice versa), AMORLINC and AMORDEGRC divide the actual days
between date_purchased and first_period by the number of days in the purchase year alone (365
or 366), rather than splitting the interval across year lengths. For example, AMORLINC(100000,
41252, 41557, 0, 0, 0.1, 1) (2012-12-09 to 2013-10-10, 305 days) computes 100000 * (0.1 * 305 /
366) = 8333.333333333334, multiplying rate by the first-period fraction before cost. For 0 <
period < 1, AMORLINC returns the full annual charge cost * rate while AMORDEGRC returns 0. All
2,957 AMORDEGRC and 4,354 AMORLINC full-bank rows match.

| `=AMORDEGRC(100380,41260,41531,0,0,0.1,1)` | as typed | `18581.0` (`0x40d2254000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

AMORLINC full-bank rows.

### FN-AND-001: AND, OR, and XOR evaluate direct arguments before references/arrays and skip direct non-boolean text unless no logical is found

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to AND, OR, XOR.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, AND, OR, and XOR inspect every argument in two passes: all direct
arguments first, then references and array constants. Direct errors therefore precede errors
inside arrays or references (AND({TRUE,#N/A},#DIV/0!) is #DIV/0!). Direct text "TRUE" and
"FALSE" parse as logicals, whereas other direct text ("x", "1", "0", "") is skipped when at
least one logical is read (AND(TRUE,"x") is TRUE, OR(FALSE,"x") is FALSE) and gives #VALUE!
when none is read (AND("x"), OR("x","y")). Inside arrays and references, all text (including
"TRUE") is skipped; omitted direct arguments read as FALSE in AND/OR and are ignored or FALSE
in XOR (XOR(TRUE,) is TRUE).

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=AND(TRUE,"x")` | as typed | `TRUE` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=AND("x")` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=AND({"TRUE"})` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=AND({TRUE,#N/A},#DIV/0!)` | as typed | `#DIV/0!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=OR(FALSE,"TRUE")` | as typed | `TRUE` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=XOR(TRUE,"x")` | as typed | `TRUE` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-AREAS-001: AREAS rejects non-reference constants at formula entry (0x800A03EC) and returns #VALUE! for runtime non-references

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, AREAS(reference) counts the disjoint areas of a reference (including
multi-area unions such as (A1:B2,C3,A4) -> 3, and single-area selections from INDEX such as

rejects literal numbers, array constants, or arithmetic expressions in its argument slot at

### FN-ASIN-001: ASIN forms u = 2 - (1 - x) rather than 1 + x, introducing a 1-ULP sign asymmetry

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ASIN(x) rejects |x| > 1 with #NUM!, evaluates t = RN53(RN64(1 - x)),
u = RN53(RN64(2 - t)), root = RN53(sqrt_x87(RN53(RN64(t * u)))), and atan_reduced(RN53(RN64(x /
root))), and flushes subnormal outputs to 0. Reusing t in 2 - t instead of computing 1 + x
independently makes ASIN(-x) differ from -ASIN(x) by 1 ULP on 714 paired inputs in the held-out
uniform capture (e.g. x = +/-0.22748320798034022). All 21,610 full-bank ASIN rows match.

### FN-ASINH-001: ASINH is LN(|x|+SQRT(x*x+1)) with every step stored, so small inputs lose their digits

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

ASINH is not the correctly rounded inverse hyperbolic sine. Its answers are those of
SIGN(x)*LN(|x|+SQRT(x*x+1)), with x*x, the +1, the SQRT and the |x|+root each rounded to 64
bits and then to 53 bits before the next step, and the LN rounded to binary64. That route loses
most of the digits of a small input: once x*x+1 rounds to 1, the answer is LN of |x|+1 after
rounding, so it moves in steps of about 2.2E-16. ASINH(-1.4901631254755754E-16) is -2.22E-16,
about 1.5 times the true value, and in the recorded rows every |x| up to 1.05E-16, including
every subnormal, gives 0 on either sign. At the other end the x*x overflows: answers are finite
up to the largest recorded input below it, 9.23E153, and #NUM! from the next recorded input,
2.38E154, although the true value there is about 356. In Excel build 20430 this route
reproduces all 4,534 recorded rows (3,017 distinct inputs): 3,427 numbers and 1,107 #NUM!. The
correctly rounded asinh matches only 1,224 of the 3,427.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |

| `ASINH(-1.4901631254755754e-16)` | number `-1.4901631254755754e-16` (`0xbca579bb4790a498`) (cells) | `-2.2204460492503128e-16` (`0xbcafffffffffffff`) | `-1.4901631254755754e-16` (`0xbca579bb4790a498`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `ASINH(1.0501151062119094e-16)` | number `1.0501151062119094e-16` (`0x3c9e447b5a2fd072`) (cells) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | `1.0501151062119094e-16` (`0x3c9e447b5a2fd072`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `ASINH(5e-324)` | number `5e-324` (`0x0000000000000001`) (cells) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | `5e-324` (`0x0000000000000001`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `ASINH(7.193439987815484e-08)` | number `7.193439987815484e-08` (`0x3e734f4b587c834b`) (cells) | `7.19343998474134e-08` (`0x3e734f4b58591206`) | `7.193439987815477e-08` (`0x3e734f4b587c8346`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `ASINH(9.234293629925394e+153)` | number `9.234293629925394e+153` (`0x5fe60a092f72d845`) (cells) | `355.2115905310072` (`0x40763362acc0ad1b`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `ASINH(2.3842260672008416e+154)` | number `2.3842260672008416e+154` (`0x5ffc73a8ae6c7c25`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | `356.1601260731963` (`0x4076428fe05b79d7`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |

Correct value: mpmath asinh at 2000 bits, rounded to the nearest binary64

Basis (measured): All 4,534 rows of two recorded sets, 3,017 and 1,517 rows, from Excel build
20430. The route was recomputed independently in exact rational arithmetic with a correctly
rounded LN, and matched every row. The stored steps matter on 5 of the rows (3 distinct
inputs): the same formula in plain binary64 misses exactly those 5.

Inferred, not measured: That Excel's code is this expression, in this order, is inferred; what
is measured is that the route reproduces every recorded row. The overflow boundary at |x| =
2^512, about 1.34E154, is inferred from x*x overflowing there: the recorded rows only bracket
it, between 9.23E153 and 2.38E154. Excel reads a subnormal written to a cell back as 0, so the
0 at subnormal inputs may come from that step and not from this route.

- Open: Only one Excel build, 20430, has been read over this range.

### FN-ATAN2-001: ATAN2 evaluates ATAN(y/x) shifted by pi, drifting by 1 ULP on 37 of 120 readings and returning #NUM! when y/x overflows

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, ATAN2(x_num, y_num) computes excel_atan(y_num / x_num) shifted by
±pi in the left half-plane (and ±pi/2 when x_num = 0, #DIV/0! at (0, 0)), rather than a
correctly rounded quadrant atan2(y, x). As a result, 37 of 120 ATAN2 readings in dcj9k_math
differ by 1 ULP from the correctly rounded mathematical value (for instance ATAN2(-0.152, 1.21)
returns 1.6957615735034952 instead of 1.6957615735034954). When x_num != 0 and y_num / x_num
overflows binary64 (e.g. ATAN2(1e-200, 1e109)), Excel returns #NUM! rather than ±pi/2.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=ATAN2(-0.152,1.21)` | as typed | `1.6957615735034952` (`0x3ffb21d6e3402d1b`) | `1.6957615735034954` (`0x3ffb21d6e3402d1c`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ATAN2(8.255,6.074)` | as typed | `0.6343487161375854` (`0x3fe44c95adc241ac`) | `0.6343487161375855` (`0x3fe44c95adc241ad`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Correct value: pi + atan(1.21 / -0.152) computed at 100 decimal digits in Python Decimal and
rounded to nearest binary64.
Correct value: atan(6.074 / 8.255) computed at 100 decimal digits in Python Decimal and rounded
to nearest binary64.

### FN-ATANH-001: ATANH has three regimes—subnormal DAZ to +0, binary64 x + x^3/3, and signed x87 ratio-log—breaking oddness above 0x3f1af82b729c1d83

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20228 and 20430, ATANH(x) returns #NUM! for |x| >= 1, flushes both signs of
any subnormal input to +0 (0x0000000000000000), evaluates ordinary binary64 x + (x*x*x)/3 for
normal |x| below 0x3f1af82b729c1d83 (~1.02880227e-4), and switches at 0x3f1af82b729c1d83 to 0.5
* LN(RN53(RN64(RN53(RN64(1+x)) / RN53(RN64(1-x))))). Because the ratio branch evaluates 1+x and
1-x directly without taking |x|, ATANH(-x) != -ATANH(x) in that regime: at ±0x3f1af82b729c1d83
the positive and negative outputs differ by 4,314 ULPs (0x3f1af82b7434c926 vs
0xbf1af82b7434b84c). All 22,008 full-bank ATANH rows match.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ATANH(5e-319)` | number `6.319821498176405e-309` (`0x00048b60699b04c8`) (cells) | `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `ATANH(1e-300)` | number `1e-300` (`0x01a56e1fc2f8f359`) (cells) | `1e-300` (`0x01a56e1fc2f8f359`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `ATANH(0.00010288022749456835)` | number `0.00010288014587100072` (`0x3f1af82b729c1d83`) (cells) | `0.000102880146233973` (`0x3f1af82b7434c926`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `ATANH(-0.00010288022749456835)` | number `-0.00010288014587100072` (`0xbf1af82b729c1d83`) (cells) | `-0.00010288014623391454` (`0xbf1af82b7434b84c`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Basis (inferred): Measured across Excel 16.0 build 20228 W109 switch/held-out campaigns

binary64 bits, so the exact switch selection between +0x3f1af82b729c1d82 and

### FN-BESSELI-001: BESSELI is ITK's published polynomial and recurrence, on the x87 unit

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

BESSELI truncates n to an integer and evaluates the body published in ITK with every operation
stored from the x87 unit at precision 64: the I0 and I1 polynomials, and for higher orders
Miller backward recurrence from j = 2*(n + int(sqrt(40*n))), rescaling by 1E-10 whenever |q| >
1E10, then normalising by I0(x). The same body in plain binary64 misses by 1 to 4 units in the
last place. The published ITK body is itkGaussianOperator.hxx at ITK
311b7060ef39e371f3cd209ec135284ff5fde735 (Apache-2.0).

### FN-BESSELI-003: At large x the fixed recurrence start makes BESSELI badly wrong

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

Excel's recurrence for orders above 1 starts at a fixed j = 2*(n + int(sqrt(40*n))), which is
far too low at large x. At x = 709.7 BESSELI of order 2 is 0.20% high, and order 3 is 53% low,
where I3(709.7) is 2.4631E306. Orders 0 and 1, which use the polynomial and not the recurrence,
are within about 1.6E-7 at the same x.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |

| `BESSELI(709.7, 3)` | x `709.7` (`0x40862d999999999a`); n `3` (`0x4008000000000000`) (cells) | `1.1560227990465618e+306` (`0x7f7a56f66ecd12a0`) | `2.4631300544524576e+306` (`0x7f8c0f97bbe572f6`) | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `BESSELI(709.7, 2)` | x `709.7` (`0x40862d999999999a`); n `2` (`0x4000000000000000`) (cells) | `2.4767103124440567e+306` (`0x7f8c3732e70ce6f9`) | `2.47182813908566e+306` (`0x7f8c28f5d197b1dd`) | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |
| `BESSELI(709.7, 0)` | x `709.7` (`0x40862d999999999a`); n `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `2.4788083687166675e+306` (`0x7f8c3d51558ee541`) | `2.4788087273156452e+306` (`0x7f8c3d519a191ac9`) | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H |

Correct value: mpmath besseli at 800 bits, order the integer part of n, correctly rounded.

Basis (measured): Readings at x = 709.7 for orders 0, 1, 2 and 3, compared with mpmath.

### FN-BESSELJ-001: BESSELJ at zero and order zero is slightly above one

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-06.*

In the retained catalogue capture, BESSELJ(0,0) returns 1.00000000283141 (0x3ff0000000c292b1),
while the mathematical Bessel function J0(0) is exactly 1. The raw answer, saved workbook cache
and answer after reopening retain that same value. This is one captured input on the named
Excel environment, not a general accuracy statement.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=BESSELJ(0,0)` | as typed | `1.00000000283141` (`0x3ff0000000c292b1`) | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA, workbook Compatibility Version 1 |

Correct value: Exact identity J0(0)=1: in the defining series in NIST DLMF 10.2.2
(https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.2#E2), only the constant term remains at order zero and x=0.

Basis (measured): One formula-literal control at sheet dc96l3_bessel, row 309, column 4 in the
landed capture. Its environment is Excel 16.0.20527.20088, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H,
en-ZA, workbook Compatibility Version 1. The raw and reopened binary64 encodings are both
3ff0000000c292b1; the saved numeric text is 1.00000000283141. The product test also pins these
result bits.

Inferred, not measured: The current published small-J0 implementation evaluates its constant
coefficients as 57568490574/57568490411 at x=0, which produces the recorded bits. That
source-level explanation does not prove that Microsoft uses the same private program.

- Open: The generic J/Y numerical bodies retain disagreements on other inputs; this control does not identify the full seed or recurrence program.

### FN-BESSELY-001: BESSELY truncates order into 0..=10,000,000 and applies a phase-shifted 2^27-1 limit that admits BESSELY(134217728, 1)

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, BESSELY(x, n) requires x > 0 and truncates n to an integer in
0..=10,000,000 (#NUM! for n < 0 such as -0.5 or n >= 10,000,001). For large x, Excel checks |x|
- phase <= 2^27 - 1 using phase = 0.785398164 for Y0 and 2.356194491 for Y1 (forward recurrence
orders require both seeds). Consequently, BESSELY(134217728, 1) is admitted and returns
1.1173873549496432e-05 (0x3ed7ff19f84f233c) because 134,217,728 - 2.356194491 <= 134,217,727,
whereas BESSELJ(134217728, 0) returns #NUM! because 134,217,728 - 0.785398164 > 134,217,727.
Subnormal operands and intermediates flush to zero.

### FN-BETA.DIST-001: The beta bgrat series stops at eps, not 15*eps, and its prefactor and ratio follow the gamma-family forms

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-11.* Applies to BETA.DIST,
BETADIST.

In the incomplete beta (TOMS 708 route) the asymptotic series bgrat is positive and truncated.
DNA Calc first ran it with the published tolerance 15*eps (1.5e-14), at which its values sat on
average 5.3 units low against BETA.DIST bank rows (mostly a > 15, b <= 1, x > 0.5, where Excel
is unbiased); running it at eps changed BETA.DIST from 982 to 1,003 matched of 2,822 (+29, -8)
and BETADIST from 140 to 142 of 294, and the mean absolute distance to Excel from 8.08 to 3.86
units, the mean signed distance from -5.31 to +0.29, rows within one unit from 1,354 to 1,432;
of tolerances tried, eps gave +23 net, 2^-52 gave +22 and 1e-17 gave +21. Three Excel 20131
rows of that block (BETA.DIST(0.9375, 20.45, 0.75), (0.96875, 61, 0.2) and (0.984375, 320,
0.05), all cumulative) were 31, 33 and 13 units low at 15*eps. A later change forms bgrat's
prefactor r as z times the gamma density at b, and u/r as one exponential of (n -
1/2)*LOG1P(b/a) - b*LOG1P((b-1)/(2a)) - b + s(n) - s(a) with the measured real-shape Stirling
errors s: BETA.DIST went from 1,003 to 1,043 matched (+75, -35) and BETADIST by +1, and the
three rows above are now 3, 5 and 3 units off. Measured and not taken: the loader beta
prefactor with a fractional-shape Stirling error (in the series arm BETA.DIST +33/-51 to
+31/-57 and FDIST +76/-147 to +65/-149; in the bup arm BETA.DIST +51/-65 to +70/-68, FDIST
+106/-63 to +96/-63, F.DIST net -3 to -5); bgrat's gamma-tail substitution alone (+28/-27, and
+81/-43 with the other two); no FDIST or F.DIST row moves in bgrat. Of the FDIST misses, 2,950
of 3,444 rows lie in the recurrence arm bup_160 and 777 of 907 in the series arm bpser; the
other arms hold fewer than 10 each.

### FN-BETA.DIST-002: Incomplete beta has no basym arm, reflects bfrac prefactors above 0.99 using caller y, and unifies bup and bgrat

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to BETA.DIST,
BETA.INV, BETADIST, BETAINV, BINOMDIST, CONFIDENCE.T, F.DIST, F.DIST.RT, FDIST, FINV,
NEGBINOM.DIST, T.DIST, T.DIST.2T, T.DIST.RT, T.INV, T.INV.2T, TDIST, TINV.

In Excel 16.0.20527, the incomplete-beta routine (bratio) removes TOMS 708's bratio_basym arm:
all min(a0, b0) > 1.0, b0 >= 40.0 inputs stay on bratio_bfrac continuously across b = 100 and
lambda = 0.03 * b (checked across 22 live bisection points). Inside bratio_bfrac, when x > 0.99
(0x3fefae147ae147ae, strict >), Excel evaluates the density prefactor as excel_brcomp(b, a, y,
x) using the caller's stored complement y rather than 1.0 - x (eliminating 53-bit cancellation
in F.DIST.RT, FDIST, and F.DIST), while keeping lam = |a - (a + b) * x| on x. bratio_bup runs
Excel's density-based stored-power recurrence for all n >= 2 (including bup_140's n = 20
shift), using ((x * y) / a) * density with stored exp(m * ln(x)) and binary64 summation for b >
1.0, and extended-precision x^m and summation for b <= 1.0 (plus excel_log(y) in
beta_density_at for a < 1 || b < 1, x > 0.99). bratio_bgrat applies the 0.99 lnx switch to all
b, evaluates seeded b == 0.5 via erf/erfc, b == 1.0 via exp(-z), and z >= 1.1 via
excel_gamma_fraction(b, z).

### FN-BIN2DEC-001: Radix converters read empty text as 0, count leading zeros toward the 10-character limit, and ignore places on negative two's-complement outputs while still validating it

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to BIN2DEC, BIN2HEX, BIN2OCT, DEC2BIN, DEC2HEX,
DEC2OCT, HEX2BIN, HEX2DEC, HEX2OCT.

Across the A-L Engineering radix converters in Excel 16.0 build 20430 and 20527, string inputs
reject any whitespace (including spaces and tabs) with #NUM!, reject logicals with #VALUE!,
count leading zeros toward the 10-character maximum (e.g. HEX2DEC("00000000001") is #NUM!),
accept lowercase hex digits, and treat the empty string "" as 0 (HEX2BIN("") = "0"). When
outputting a negative number in two's complement, Excel always emits 10 digits regardless of
places (DEC2BIN(-512, 1) = "1000000000"), yet still requires an explicit places argument to
truncate into 1..=10 (#NUM! for 0 or 11).

### FN-BINOM.DIST.RANGE-001: BINOM.DIST.RANGE with s < s2 evaluates the stored CDF difference rather than summing masses

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

When number_s < number_s2 and 0 < probability_s < 1, BINOM.DIST.RANGE(trials, probability_s,
number_s, [number_s2]) truncates trials, number_s, and number_s2 and evaluates
RN53(RN64(BINOM.DIST(s2, n, p, TRUE) - BINOM.DIST(s - 1, n, p, TRUE))) (or the upper tail
directly when s = 0) rather than summing individual probability masses, with subnormal results
flushed to 0. All 1,224 full-bank BINOM.DIST.RANGE rows match.

| `=BINOM.DIST.RANGE(60,0.75,45,50)` | as typed | `0.5236297934718872` (`0x3fe0c19344c58922`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-BINOM.INV-001: BINOM.INV and CRITBINOM test the public cumulative: strictly at zero successes, inclusively at later counts

*Quirk; inferred; recorded 2026-11-11.* Applies to BINOM.INV, CRITBINOM.

On Excel 16.0.20527, 252 dyadic boundary designs were each asked at the exact lower tail of the
binomial and at three binary64 neighbours either side. Of these, the 200 designs whose answer
is a count above zero return k exactly when BINOM.DIST(k, n, p, TRUE) >= alpha, that is the
smallest k whose public cumulative probability reaches alpha. The 52 designs whose answer is
zero return 0 only when BINOM.DIST(0, n, p, TRUE) > alpha, so the mass at zero is compared
strictly and every later cumulative inclusively. DNA Calc locates the count with a forward mass
recurrence and settles it with these two public-tail comparisons; with that, BINOM.INV went
from 2,290 to 2,302 of 2,308 and CRITBINOM from 1,402 to 1,414 of 1,420 full-bank rows matched,
13 won and 1 lost in each function. The lost row is (5, 0.5, 0.5).

| `BINOM.INV(1, 0.5, 0.1)` | trials `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); probability_s `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`); alpha `0.1` (`0x3fb999999999999a`) (cells) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `BINOM.INV(1, 0.5, 0.5)` | trials `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); probability_s `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`); alpha `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`) (cells) | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Basis (inferred): The 252-design reading and its two comparison rules are quoted from the doc
comment of the DnaCalc kernel, which cites Excel 16.0.20527; the two cited rows (build 20430)
show the zero-count answer at alpha 0.5 for one trial and do not test the inclusive rule above
zero, which no cited row locates. Counts are from the commit message and bead comment.

Inferred, not measured: The rule is stated as a description of the 252 designs; that it holds
for every n, p and alpha is not shown.

- Open: The row (5, 0.5, 0.5), matched before and lost after the change, in both functions.
- Open: The six BINOM.INV and six CRITBINOM bank rows still unmatched.

### FN-BITAND-001: Bitwise functions reject fractional operands with #NUM! instead of truncating them, while shift counts truncate

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to BITAND, BITLSHIFT, BITOR, BITRSHIFT, BITXOR.

already be integers in [0, 2^48 - 1]; any fractional part (such as 0.1 or 1.5) returns #NUM!

### FN-BITLSHIFT-001: BITLSHIFT and BITRSHIFT return 0 for |shift_amount| in 49..=53 and bypass the shift-count bound when number is 0

*Documentation differs from behaviour; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to BITLSHIFT,
BITRSHIFT.

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, BITLSHIFT and BITRSHIFT deviate from Microsoft's published 48-bit
result and 53-bit shift limits in two ways: (1) when number is 0, any finite shift_amount
returns 0 (even BITLSHIFT(0, 54) = 0); (2) when number is nonzero and the truncated
|shift_amount| is 49..=53, both functions return 0 instead of #NUM! (e.g. BITLSHIFT(1, 49) = 0
and BITLSHIFT(1, 53) = 0, whereas BITLSHIFT(1, 48) = #NUM! and BITLSHIFT(1, 54) = #NUM!).

Documentation: Microsoft's BITLSHIFT and BITRSHIFT pages state that if the result exceeds 2^48
- 1 (48 bits) or |shift_amount| > 53, the functions return #NUM!, without noting that zero
operands ignore finite shift_amount > 53 or that |shift_amount| in 49..=53 returns 0 instead of
#NUM!.
(https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/bitlshift-function-c55bb27e-cacd-4c7c-b258-d80861a03c9c;
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/bitrshift-function-274d6996-f42c-4743-abdb-4ff95351222c)

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BITLSHIFT(1, 48)` | number `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); shift_amount `48.0` (`0x4048000000000000`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `BITLSHIFT(1, 49)` | number `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); shift_amount `49.0` (`0x4048800000000000`) (cells) | `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `BITLSHIFT(1, 53)` | number `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); shift_amount `53.0` (`0x404a800000000000`) (cells) | `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `BITLSHIFT(0, 54)` | number `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`); shift_amount `54.0` (`0x404b000000000000`) (cells) | `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `BITRSHIFT(1, -53)` | number `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); shift_amount `-53.0` (`0xc04a800000000000`) (cells) | `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

### FN-CELL-001: CELL does not trim info_type, reads the active cell when reference is omitted, and returns a two-element {width, is_default} array for "width"

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, CELL matches info_type case-insensitively without trimming
whitespace (so CELL(" format ", B2) is #VALUE!). Omitting reference reads the workbook's active
cell (so CELL("address") on another sheet returns the active sheet and cell such as
[oracle.xlsx]Data!$A$1). CELL("width", ref) returns a 1x2 array {width, is_default} where width
is the rounded column width (0 when hidden) and is_default is TRUE/FALSE; legacy formulas
implicitly intersect this array to the width number. CELL("prefix", ref) emits ', ", ^, or \
only for text constants and "" for numbers, formulas, logicals, errors, and blanks.

### FN-CHAR-001: CHAR and CODE use the Windows-1252 code page (CHAR(128) is U+20AC, astral characters give CODE 63), while UNICHAR/UNICODE use Unicode scalar values

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to CHAR, CODE, UNICHAR, UNICODE.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (UI language 1033 / en-ZA), CHAR maps 1..=255 through Windows-1252
rather than ISO-8859-1, so CHAR(128) is '€' (U+20AC) and CHAR(159) is 'Ÿ' (U+0178). CODE("")
returns #VALUE!, and characters outside Windows-1252 such as an astral emoji
(LEFT(UNICHAR(128512),1)) return 63 ('?'), whereas UNICHAR and UNICODE preserve full Unicode
scalar values (UNICODE(LEFT(UNICHAR(128512),1)) = 128512).

### FN-CHOOSEROWS-001: CHOOSEROWS counts negative selectors from the bottom, flattens array selectors row-major, and rejects 0 or out-of-bounds with #VALUE!

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527, CHOOSEROWS(array, row_num1, ...) selects 1-based rows in the order given
(permitting duplicates and reordering), counts negative selectors from the last row (-1 selects
the final row), truncates fractional selectors toward zero, flattens array selectors in
row-major order, and returns #VALUE! when any selector is 0 or its magnitude exceeds the
array's row count. All 3,000 full-bank CHOOSEROWS rows match.

### FN-COLUMN-001: COLUMN spills a horizontal array for multi-column ranges, #SPILL! on whole-row ranges off column A, and rejects non-reference constants at entry (0x800A03EC)

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527, COLUMN([reference]) without an argument returns the calling cell's 1-based
column (COLUMN() at Sheet1!H10 -> 8, at XFD1048576 -> 16384). For a multi-column single-area

### FN-COMBIN-001: COMBIN and COMBINA return 83.99999999999999 (1 ULP below 84) for C(9, 3) via cyclic x87-stored factors with * n last

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to COMBIN,
COMBINA.

In Excel 16.0 build 20228, COMBIN(n, k) truncates n and k (with subnormals treated as signed
zero and n <= 2,147,483,646), reduces k = min(k, n - k), and evaluates product(i=2..=k,
(n-k+i-1)/i) * n, storing every division and accumulator product from x87 PC64 to binary64 and
multiplying n last. Because 7/2 * 8/3 * 9 divides by 3 before multiplying by 9, COMBIN(9, 3)
and COMBINA(7, 3) return 83.99999999999999 (0x4054ffffffffffff) instead of exact 84
(0x4055000000000000). COMBINA truncates its two arguments independently before forming total =
trunc(n) + trunc(k) - 1 and evaluates trunc(n) == 0 && trunc(k) == 0 -> 1 before checking
negative k, so COMBINA(-0.25, 0.75) returns 1.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COMBIN(9, 3)` | number `9.0` (`0x4022000000000000`); number_chosen `3.0` (`0x4008000000000000`) (cells) | `83.99999999999999` (`0x4054ffffffffffff`) | `84.0` (`0x4055000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `COMBINA(7, 3)` | number `7.0` (`0x401c000000000000`); number_chosen `3.0` (`0x4008000000000000`) (cells) | `83.99999999999999` (`0x4054ffffffffffff`) | `84.0` (`0x4055000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `COMBINA(-0.25, 0.75)` | number `-0.25` (`0xbfd0000000000000`); number_chosen `0.75` (`0x3fe8000000000000`) (cells) | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Correct value: Exact integer combinatorics: C(9, 3) = 9*8*7 / 6 = 84.
Correct value: Exact integer combinatorics: C(7+3-1, 3) = C(9, 3) = 84.

Basis (measured): Measured across 20,713 COMBIN discovery rows, 1,024 cyclic held-out rows, and
35,233 COMBINA identity rows in Excel 16.0 build 20228 (CalcFunc-Evidence
work/w109/G4-04-combin/ and G4-04-combina/), and matched on 25,199/25,199 COMBIN and
40,991/40,991 COMBINA full-bank rows.

### FN-COMPLEX-001: COMPLEX formats coefficients to 15 digits via directed x87 rounding, turns DBL_MIN into "0", and rejects DBL_MAX

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, COMPLEX(real_num, i_num, [suffix]) formats each nonzero
coefficient to 15 significant digits via ExactDecimal::fifteen_x87 (floor(frexp_k / 3.3219),

### FN-CONCAT-001: Number-to-text emits 15 significant digits via an exact Q16.64 split on [1, 65536) and x87 low-nibble scaling into Q0.64 elsewhere

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to ARRAYTOTEXT,
CONCAT, CONCATENATE, DOLLAR, FIXED, OP_CONCAT, TEXT, TEXTJOIN, VALUETOTEXT.

Every worksheet consumer of general 15-significant-digit number-to-text conversion (&, CONCAT,
CONCATENATE, VALUETOTEXT, ARRAYTOTEXT, FIXED, DOLLAR, TEXT, TEXTJOIN, and general cell
formatting) shares one routine (first_precision). For 1.0 <= |x| < 65,536.0 (0 <= exp2 < 16),
Branch 1 splits the binary64 significand directly into an integer part w (1..=65535, d digits)
and an exact Q0.64 fraction f with no FPU scaling, then adds the truncated half-ulp constant
floor(2^63 / 10^(15 - d)); because floor(2^63 / 10^k) < 2^63 / 10^k, exact binary ties below
65,536 never round up, and [1, 10) rounds up only past +0.07204 ulp64(v). For |x| < 1.0 or |x|
>= 65,536.0, Branch 2 computes p = ceil((exp2 + 1) / 3.3219) (0 for [0.5, 1)), multiplies x by
10^-p using the low-nibble-first x87 PC64 table chain (10^+-1..15, 10^+-16..240, 10^+-256) with
one 10^-1 step if scaled v >= 1.0, shifts the 64-bit significand mv into Q0.64 by a truncating
right shift, and adds floor(2^63 / 10^k) (k in 15..=17). That explains why [0.5, 1) and
below-2^k values require +0.372036854775808 ulp64(v) to round up, while above-2^k values
exhibit a period-8 oscillation +3.37203685 + 1.25 * (mv & 7) ulp64(10v). See
https://github.com/DnaCalc/DnaCalc/blob/344d70dcea3ea77cbbeee1595f96694630a9610a/docs/articles/last-bit-number-text.md.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CONCAT(3.645252540996335, "")` | text1 `3.645252540996335` (`0x400d297a2a09ebd8`); text2 `` (cells) | `3.64525254099634` | Excel 16.0.20527.20196, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |
| `CONCAT(86497.03926400005, "")` | text1 `86497.03926400005` (`0x40f51e10a0d349c2`); text2 `` (cells) | `86497.0392640001` | Excel 16.0.20527.20196, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |
| `CONCAT(8.594243319945645e-293, "")` | text1 `8.594243319945645e-293` (`0x034b71c2dc7a8ed6`); text2 `` (cells) | `8.5942433199457E-293` | Excel 16.0.20527.20196, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |

Basis (inferred): Measured on 21,377 probe and W111 rows (21,377 of 21,377 matched), 29
formerly failing oracle-corpus cells (29 of 29 matched across dc_q9rb, catalogue, and
fn7_format_context), and three prospective frozen proofs in nx8 on Excel 16.0.20527.20196: 600
of 600 on frozen_cb9_predictions.jsonl, 32 of 32 on the 4-binade discriminator (exp2 in {-971,
-486, +484, +969}, settling ceil(frexp_k / 3.3219) 32/32 vs ceil(frexp_k * log10(2)) 0/32), and

Inferred, not measured: Whether Excel implements Branch 1 via integer bit-shifts or x87
fistp+fsub is unobservable from outputs and inferred; both give identical (w, f) for every
binary64 in [1.0, 65536.0).

### FN-CONVERT-001: CONVERT evaluates linear units via a three-store x87 PC64 chain, treats bar as #N/A, and uses direct affine temperature pairs

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20228 and 20527, CONVERT(number, from_unit, to_unit) evaluates supported
linear categories via three x87 PC64 operations each stored to binary64 before the next:
RN53(RN64(RN53(RN64(number * from_factor)) / to_factor) * decimal_prefix_delta), where
decimal_prefix_delta is the single binary64 power 10^(from_exp - to_exp) rather than a quotient
of prefix factors; length factors use exact integer angstroms, pressure stores independent
reciprocals of units-per-pascal while rejecting bar with #N/A, and K/C/F use six direct affine
formulas. Matches 33,972/33,972 full-bank and 120/120 pinned CONVERT rows.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |

### FN-CORREL-001: CORREL and PEARSON use population normalisation (n) with stored-PC64 two-pass arithmetic, while RSQ squares the sample-normalised (n-1) correlation

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to CORREL, PEARSON,
RSQ.

In Excel 16.0.20527 (dc-wli1), CORREL and PEARSON divide centred sums of squares and
cross-products by n (population variance/covariance) using x87 64-bit intermediate
additions/products stored to binary64 at each step in the first-pass means, second-pass centred
sums, roots, and final division. By contrast, RSQ squares the sample-normalised (n-1)
correlation in binary64, so mathematically equivalent three-point inputs produce distinct last
bits in RSQ (0x3fdb6db6db6db6da vs 0x3fdb6db6db6db6dd) while CORREL and PEARSON match
0x3fe4f2ec413cb52b.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=CORREL(Data!A1:A3,Data!E1:E3)` | as typed | `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (inferred): Measured across 414 identification/holdout vectors, 92 accumulation controls,
47 precision holdout vectors, and 438 corpus CORREL cells in Excel 16.0.20527
(docs/research/correlation-arithmetic-2026-11-12.md), plus 2,853/2,853 CORREL, 2,854/2,854
PEARSON, and 2,852/2,852 RSQ full-bank rows.

Inferred, not measured: That the stored-PC64 operation graph holds for all vector lengths
beyond the mined holdout controls (with integer division by n indistinguishable on small
counts) is inferred from dc-wli1; the raw probe JSONs were archived to R2 rather than
committed.

Evidence:

- DnaCalc `docs/research/correlation-arithmetic-2026-11-12.md` at `4fb9b728df` — dc-wli1 CORREL, PEARSON, and RSQ identification and precision holdouts
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/src/ported/paired_stats_common.rs` at `4fb9b728df` — Two-pass population CORREL/PEARSON and sample RSQ implementation
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/tests/f1_stats.rs`, correlation_population_normalisation_and_rsq_sample_normalisation at `4fb9b728df` — Three-point CORREL/PEARSON vs RSQ discriminators
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/tests/captures/catalogue/sections/prefix_metadata.capture.json`, sheet prefix_metadata row 51 column 1 at `4fb9b728df` (readings)

### FN-COSH-001: COSH evaluates (EXP(x) + EXP(-x))/2 via stored x87 addition, returning #NUM! above ln(DBL_MAX) where cosh(x) is still finite

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, COSH(x) computes RN53(RN64(EXP(x) + EXP(-x))) / 2 using Excel's
worksheet EXP kernel rather than calling the Windows CRT cosh() (which differs by 1 ULP on 29
of 1,224 W111 extended-numeric rows, and at 0.001, 0.01, and 10). Because EXP(|x|) overflows
binary64 around 709.7827, COSH(-709.7827128933891) returns #NUM! even though the mathematical
cosh is ~8.98846567435735e+307, half of DBL_MAX. All 33,550 full-bank COSH rows match.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COSH(-709.7827128933891)` | number `-709.7827128933891` (`0xc0862e42fefa3a1c`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | `8.98846567435735e+307` (`0x7fe0000000005995`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `COSH(0.29241103248877653)` | number `0.29241103248877653` (`0x3fd2b6dcc361d950`) (cells) | `1.043057599268652` (`0x3ff0b05d2a4b4009`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

Correct value: cosh(|-709.7827128933891|) = (exp(|x|) + exp(-|x|))/2 computed at 120 decimal
digits in Python Decimal and rounded to nearest binary64.

Basis (measured): Measured across Excel 16.0 build 20430 extended-numeric and
integer-hyperbolic held-out captures in CalcFunc-Evidence and matched on 33,550/33,550
full-bank COSH rows.

Evidence:

- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/src/ported/cosh.rs`, cosh_kernel at `95eb0cb2ef` — (EXP(x) + EXP(-x))/2 staged x87 addition
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/witness-status.tsv`, COSH at `95eb0cb2ef` — 33,550/33,550 full-bank COSH matches
- CalcFunc-Evidence `runs/w111-integer-hyperbolic-heldout-20260929/answers/answers-cosh.json.gz`, w111inthyp-heldout-COSH-005172 at `4ef2c244d7` (readings)

### FN-COUPDAYS-001: On basis 1 COUPDAYS walks back from maturity by its own rule, not COUPPCD to COUPNCD

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to COUPDAYS, COUPNCD, COUPPCD.

On basis 1 (actual/actual) COUPDAYS does not always equal COUPNCD minus COUPPCD. Its rule:
start at maturity and step back by 12/frequency months. Each step keeps the day of the month
and clamps it to the length of the target month, and the clamped date is the start of the next
step, so passing through February lowers the day for every earlier date. Stop at the last date
still after settlement, call it next. The answer is the number of actual days from one period
before next up to next, and this last step keeps month ends: if next is the last day of its
month, the start is the last day of its month. On the other bases the answer is 360/frequency
(bases 0, 2, 4) or 365/frequency (basis 3). With this rule, all 5,584 recorded rows match
(4,072 distinct inputs): 5,568 numbers and 16 #NUM!, from Excel builds 20131 and 20430. Of the
967 basis 1 rows, 81 (49 distinct inputs) differ from the day count between the dates of a
schedule anchored on maturity with month ends kept. For maturity 1998-06-30 with semi-annual
coupons, COUPDAYS(35748,35976,2,1) is 183, from 1997-06-30 to 1997-12-30; the anchored schedule
gives 184. In one recorded case all three functions were read on the same inputs:
COUPNCD(44043,2958465,2,1) less COUPPCD is 44196 - 44012 = 184, and COUPDAYS is 183.

### FN-COUPDAYSNC-001: On basis 0 COUPDAYSNC is not always COUPDAYS minus COUPDAYBS

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to COUPDAYBS, COUPDAYS, COUPDAYSNC.

On basis 0 (US 30/360), COUPDAYSNC is P - A. A is COUPDAYBS, the accrued days. P is a 30/360
count between the actual previous and next coupon dates, with day 31 and the last day of
February both counted as day 30. COUPDAYS on basis 0 is always 360/frequency, but P need not
be: when a coupon falls on the last day of February and maturity is not a month end, P can be
88, 89 or 92 for a quarter and 178 or 182 for a half year. So COUPDAYSNC(39923,50919,4,0), with
coupons 2009-02-28 and 2009-05-29, is 39: P is 89 and A is 50, where 90 - 50 would give 40.
With no coupon date before settlement in Excel's calendar, the period starts at serial 0:
COUPDAYSNC(33,400,2,0) is 1, and for settlement 61, maturity 456 and annual coupons COUPDAYBS
plus COUPDAYSNC is 90, not 360. This rule matches all 1,664 recorded number rows on basis 0,
733 of them chosen near February, month ends and the start of the calendar.

### FN-COUPNUM-001: COUPNUM is #NUM! when the coupon before settlement falls before 1900

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to COUPNCD, COUPNUM, COUPPCD.

If the coupon date before settlement, counted back from maturity, falls before 1 January 1900,
COUPNUM gives #NUM!. The other coupon functions still answer for the same inputs: COUPPCD
returns 0, COUPNCD the next coupon, and COUPDAYS, COUPDAYBS and COUPDAYSNC a day count. With
maturity serial 400 (1901-02-03) and semi-annual coupons, the coupon dates are serials 34 and
216: settlement 33 gives #NUM!, settlement 34 gives 2. With maturity 367, settlement 0 gives

### FN-COVAR-001: COVAR, COVARIANCE.P, and COVARIANCE.S skip non-numeric pairs, validate singletons before shape, and center via two-pass means

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to COVAR,
COVARIANCE.P, COVARIANCE.S.

In Excel 16.0.20527, COVAR(array1, array2), COVARIANCE.P(array1, array2), and
COVARIANCE.S(array1, array2) validate single-cell blank/error arguments in formula order before
checking array shape (#N/A on mismatch), skip positions where either input holds text, logical,
or blank, and compute sum((x - mean_x) * (y - mean_y)) / denom in binary64 from two-pass sample
means: COVAR and COVARIANCE.P divide by n (returning 0 for 1 numeric pair and #DIV/0! for 0
pairs), whereas COVARIANCE.S divides by n - 1 (returning #DIV/0! when fewer than 2 numeric
pairs exist). Matches 2,855/2,855 COVAR, 2,849/2,849 COVARIANCE.P, and 2,850/2,850 COVARIANCE.S
full-bank rows.

| `=COVARIANCE.S(Data!A1:A3,Data!E1:E3)` | as typed | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-CUBEKPIMEMBER-001: CUBEKPIMEMBER validates scalar errors and numeric kpi_property text before connection lookup, returning #VALUE! for invalid text and #N/A on models without KPIs

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527, CUBEKPIMEMBER(connection, kpi_name, kpi_property, [caption]) checks scalar
errors on connection, kpi_name, and kpi_property first, then validates that kpi_property is

### FN-CUBEVALUE-001: CUBEVALUE sums <=6-decimal columns as exact scaled integers, returns 1 without a measure, returns "" on empty slices, and rejects duplicate hierarchies with #VALUE!

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527, CUBEVALUE(connection, [member_expression1], ...) evaluates SUM over a
workbook data model column whose entries all have at most 6 decimal places as an exact scaled
integer rounded once to binary64 (returning 42.3, 0x4045266666666666, for {10, 20, 5, 7, 0.1,

measure it returns 1; with an empty slice it returns ""; when given a CUBESET it sums across
the set's members; two members from one hierarchy or two measures return #VALUE!; and numbers
or "" return #N/A. All 4,246 full-bank CUBEVALUE rows match.

### FN-CUMPRINC-001: CUMPRINC follows PPMT on one loan and not in general; its own route is open

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to CUMIPMT,
CUMPRINC.

On the 30-year loan, CUMPRINC(0.05/12,360,200000,1,12,0) equals the left-to-right binary64 sum
of Excel's own twelve PPMT answers, to the last bit, and CUMIPMT over the same periods equals
12*PMT - CUMPRINC, computed from Excel's own answers, to the last bit. That does not
generalise: over recorded type 0 calls for a single period, CUMPRINC equals PPMT on 56 of 135
rows and differs on 79, with PPMT computed by the route in FN-IPMT-001.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=CUMPRINC(0.05/12,360,200000,1,12,0)` | as typed | `-2950.7306911349597` (`0xc0a70d761d260042`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=CUMIPMT(0.05/12,360,200000,1,12,0)` | as typed | `-9932.988261156377` (`0xc0c3667e7f577146`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=PMT(0.05/12,360,200000)` | as typed | `-1073.6432460242781` (`0xc090c692af15f63a`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): One loan block of the catalogue capture, recomputed from the recorded answers
by binary64 arithmetic, and 135 recorded single-period CUMPRINC rows compared with PPMT's
route.

Inferred, not measured: That the 79 single-period differences are CUMPRINC's own and not PPMT's
rests on the PPMT route, which matches every fv 0, type 0 row tested. That CUMIPMT remains
count*PMT less CUMPRINC beyond this block is inferred.

- Open: CUMPRINC's per-period route. Recurrences, closed balances, count*PMT less interest and binary64 variants all stay below PPMT's 56 of 135. Recorded rows now match CUMPRINC 185 of 586 and CUMIPMT 12 of 38.

### FN-DATE-001: In the 1900 date system, serial 0 is 1900-01-00 and serial 60 is the fictitious 1900-02-29

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to DATE, DAY, DAYS, EDATE, EOMONTH, MONTH,
WEEKDAY, YEAR.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088 under the 1900 date system, serial 0 formats as 1900/1/0
(YEAR(0)=1900, MONTH(0)=1, DAY(0)=0), and 1900 is treated as a leap year so DATE(1900,2,29)
returns 60, WEEKDAY(60,2) returns 3 (Wednesday), and DATE(1900,3,1)-DATE(1900,2,28) returns 2.
EOMONTH(60,0) returns 59 (1900-02-28) rather than 60, whereas EDATE(60,12) returns 425
(1901-02-28).

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=YEAR(0)&"/"&MONTH(0)&"/"&DAY(0)` | as typed | `1900/1/0` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=DATE(1900,2,29)` | as typed | `60.0` (`0x404e000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-DATE-002: Excel 16.0.20527 rejects DATE with year >= 10000 even when negative month/day offsets roll back below 10000, differing from build 20430

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

Across 22 witness rows in crates/calc-func/witness-differences.tsv, Excel 16.0.20430 rolled
negative month or day offsets back from year 10000 (or 9999.9999999) into 9999 and returned a
valid serial (for example DATE(10000, 0, 0) = 2958434, 9999-11-30), whereas Excel 16.0.20527
rejects year >= 10000 before month/day normalization and returns #NUM! on all 22 rows.

### FN-DATEDIF-001: DATEDIF unit "MD" can return negative day counts when crossing a shorter preceding month

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, DATEDIF(start_date, end_date, unit) truncates both serials, rejects
start_date > end_date or unknown unit strings (anything outside trimmed case-insensitive Y, M,
D, YM, YD, MD) with #NUM!, and for unit "MD" when end_day < start_day computes end_day +
days_in_previous_month(end_year, end_month) - start_day. When start_day exceeds the month
preceding end_date (e.g. 2001-01-31 to 2001-03-01, crossing 28-day February), "MD" returns -2
(and 2001-01-30 to 2001-03-01 returns -1). All 2,914 full-bank DATEDIF rows match.

### FN-DAYS360-001: DAYS360 treats serial 60 as 1900-02-29 and differs by 1 day on leap-Feb-29 to non-leap-Feb-28

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In the 1900 date system, DAYS360(start_date, end_date, [method]) maps serial 60 to the
fictitious 1900-02-29 and truncates fractional serials. On 2024-02-29 (serial 45351) to
2025-02-28 (serial 45716), Excel 16.0.20527.20088 returns 358 under the US/NASD method
(FALSE/omitted) and 359 under the European method (TRUE), because US/NASD adjusts start day 29
to 30 while leaving non-leap end day 28 unadjusted when both dates are end-of-February. All
4,564 full-bank DAYS360 rows match.

### FN-DB-001: DB keeps life fractional while truncating period/month, rounds rate via decimal ROUND, and flushes subnormal steps

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, DB(cost, salvage, life, period, [month]) truncates period and month
toward zero while leaving life fractional (so DB(1000, 100, 0.5, 0.25, 1) computes rate = 1 -
(100/1000)^(1/0.5) = 0.99 and returns 82.5). The depreciation rate is rounded to 3 decimal
places using Excel's 15-significant-digit decimal ROUND rule, integer-power exponents below
u32::MAX use an x87 loop, an overflowing exp/log rate power yielding NaN produces rate 0, and
each period's depreciation is flushed from subnormals to 0 before updating book value. All
2,034 full-bank DB rows match.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DB(1000, 100, 0.5, 0.25, 1)` | cost `1000.0` (`0x408f400000000000`); salvage `100.0` (`0x4059000000000000`); life `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`); period `0.25` (`0x3fd0000000000000`); month `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) (cells) | `82.5` (`0x4054a00000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `=DB(1000000,100000,6,7,7)` | as typed | `15845.098473848073` (`0x40cef28c9aca827e`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): Measured across CalcFunc-Evidence
cache/w111-depreciation-20260929/answers-db.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and Excel
16.0.20527.20088 (f3_financial row 7); 2,034/2,034 full-bank rows match.

### FN-DCOUNTA-001: DCOUNTA counts non-blank matching cells (or records when field is omitted), requires 2+ rows in database/criteria, and rejects non-reference databases at entry (0x800A03EC)

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

records when field is omitted), matches un-operatored text criteria as case-insensitive

### FN-DDB-001: DDB flushes subnormal factor/life before multiplying by cost and uses a u32::MAX integer-power threshold

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, DDB(cost, salvage, life, period, [factor]) evaluates rate =
RN53(RN64(factor / life)) and flushes a subnormal rate to 0 before multiplying by cost,
evaluates (1 - rate)^(period - 1) via an x87-stored binary-squaring loop when period - 1 is an
integer below u32::MAX (and via excel_pow_positive at or above u32::MAX), and checks
declining-amount overflow before clipping to salvage. All 1,761 full-bank DDB rows match.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DDB(1000, 100, 1.5, 1.1, 0.5)` | cost `1000.0` (`0x408f400000000000`); salvage `100.0` (`0x4059000000000000`); life `1.5` (`0x3ff8000000000000`); period `1.1` (`0x3ff199999999999a`); factor `0.5` (`0x3fe0000000000000`) (cells) | `320.08816693073936` (`0x4074016921ba41d4`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |
| `=DDB(2400,300,10,2)` | as typed | `384.0` (`0x4078000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (inferred): Measured in CalcFunc-Evidence
cache/w111-depreciation-20260929/answers-ddb.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and Excel
16.0.20527.20088 (f3_financial row 9); 1,761/1,761 full-bank rows match.

### FN-DECIMAL-001: DECIMAL strips leading whitespace only, treats empty text as 0, and rejects trailing whitespace, signs, or radix outside 2..36

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

### FN-DELTA-001: DELTA and GESTEP read their second argument first

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to DELTA, ERF, GESTEP.

When both arguments of DELTA or GESTEP are bad, the error comes from the second one:
DELTA(TRUE,#REF!) is #REF! and DELTA(#REF!,TRUE) is #VALUE!. With two errors, DELTA gives the
second. ERF reads left to right: ERF(TRUE,#REF!) is #VALUE! and ERF(#REF!,TRUE) is #REF!. A
logical is rejected in either position of these functions, whether typed or held in a cell:
DELTA(TRUE,0) and DELTA(2,TRUE) are #VALUE!, and DELTA(B1,0) with TRUE in B1 is #VALUE!, while
an empty B1 reads as 0 and gives 1.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=DELTA(TRUE,#REF!)` | as typed | `#REF!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=DELTA(#REF!,TRUE)` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=GESTEP(TRUE,#REF!)` | as typed | `#REF!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=GESTEP(#REF!,TRUE)` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ERF(TRUE,#REF!)` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ERF(#REF!,TRUE)` | as typed | `#REF!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `DELTA(A1, A2)` | number1 `#N/A`; number2 `#REF!` (cells) | `#REF!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088, Windows, bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading file |
| `=DELTA(B1,0)` | B1 `TRUE` (cells) | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=DELTA(B1,0)` | B1 `(empty cell)` (cells) | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): 16 recorded DELTA and GESTEP formula readings, 8 readings each with errors
and text held in cells, and the ERF companions on the same sheets. GESTEP gave the same pattern

### FN-DEVSQ-001: DEVSQ squares deviations with x87 multiplication and flushes subnormal squares to 0 before summing

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, DEVSQ computes the sample mean in binary64, forms each
squared deviation RN53(RN64((v - mean) * (v - mean))) on the x87 unit, and flushes any
subnormal square below DBL_MIN to 0 before summing (so DEVSQ(8.08239784871588e-295,
9.013847760079092e-295) returns 0). All 23,106 full-bank DEVSQ rows match.

### FN-DISC-001: The discount-security functions run a fixed formula order on the x87 unit

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to DISC, INTRATE,
PRICEDISC, RECEIVED, TBILLYIELD.

With B the year basis and D the day count, Excel evaluates DISC = (1 - pr/red) * (B/D); INTRATE
= ((red - inv)/inv) * (B/D); RECEIVED = inv / (1 - (disc*D)/B); PRICEDISC = red -
((disc*red)*D)/B; TBILLYIELD = ((100 - pr)/pr) * (360/D), each + - * / taken from the x87 unit
at precision 64 and stored to binary64. Results can sit several units from the exact value: the
DISC row below is 5 units below it.

### FN-DOLLARDE-001: DOLLARDE and DOLLARFR scale by 10^ceil(log10(d)) and keep truncated fraction as binary64

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to DOLLARDE, DOLLARFR.

In Excel 16.0 build 20430, DOLLARDE and DOLLARFR truncate fraction toward zero as binary64
(avoiding 32-bit integer saturation, so DOLLARDE(1.5, 1e10) returns 1.5), reject negative
fraction with #NUM! and truncated 0 with #DIV/0!, and scale the fractional part using
10^ceil(log10(d)) rather than 10^(digit count). Consequently, any power-of-10 denominator (1,
10, 100, 1e10) equals its scale and leaves the input number unchanged. All 4,847 DOLLARDE and
3,641 DOLLARFR full-bank rows match.

| `DOLLARFR(321.7284820001346, 100)` | decimal_dollar `321.7284820001346` (`0x40741ba7dcbde4d8`); fraction `100.0` (`0x4059000000000000`) (cells) | `321.7284820001346` (`0x40741ba7dcbde4d8`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |

### FN-DSTDEV-001: DSTDEV, DSTDEVP, DVAR, and DVARP compute variance via raw x87 PC64-stored moments with centered fallback, returning #DIV/0! on <2 (sample) or 0 (population) numbers

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to DSTDEV, DSTDEVP,
DVAR, DVARP.

In Excel 16.0.20527, DSTDEV, DSTDEVP, DVAR, and DVARP collect numbers in matching records'
field cells (ignoring text, logicals, and blanks while propagating errors), reject
non-reference database arguments at formula entry (0x800A03EC), return #DIV/0! on 0 matching
numbers (and on 1 matching number for sample DSTDEV/DVAR, whereas population DSTDEVP/DVARP
return 0), and evaluate variance through Excel's x87 PC64-stored raw-moment sequence (switching
to centered deviations when square_total / count / squares > 0.99, variance * 1000 <= |mean|,
or non-finite, with staged sqrt for DSTDEV/DSTDEVP). All 6,507 DSTDEV, 5,673 DSTDEVP, 5,669
DVAR, and 5,670 DVARP full-bank rows match.

### FN-DURATION-001: DURATION and MDURATION time the redemption at S(S(off+n)-1); a one-coupon bond is not a special case

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-11.* Applies to DURATION,
MDURATION.

DNA Calc's DURATION and MDURATION give the redemption cash flow the time t = S(S(off + n) - 1),
with off the fraction (E - A) / E of the first period still to run, n the number of coupons
left and S the store of the x87 running sum to binary64: the sum off + n is stored, then 1 is
subtracted. The earlier form, off + (n - 1), differs from it whenever the sum crosses a binade,
and on the recorded rows every DURATION and MDURATION miss with n greater than 1 had the two
values different while none of the 7,908 rows where they agree was a miss. A bond with one
coupon left is no longer answered as off / frequency regardless of yield: it runs the same
weighted ratio, so its answer depends on the yield (8 DURATION and 7 MDURATION recorded rows).
Against the full bank of recorded rows this took DURATION from 7,707 to 7,859 matched of 7,884
and MDURATION from 1,113 to 1,238 matched of 1,260, with no row lost in either function.
Variants that were measured and not taken: the stored time on the redemption only (7,851 and
1,231 matched); the redemption weight and the discount exponent both changed (7,710 and 1,113);
every coupon weight changed (7,781 and 1,222); every weight and exponent (7,691 and 1,111);
every weight with the one-coupon change (7,788 and 1,228). After the change 25 DURATION and 22
MDURATION bank rows are still unmatched.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DURATION(46356, 46446, 0.05, 0.005, 2, 2)` | settlement `46356` (`0x40e6a28000000000`); maturity `46446` (`0x40e6adc000000000`); rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); yld `0.005` (`0x3f747ae147ae147b`); frequency `2` (`0x4000000000000000`); basis `2` (`0x4000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.24722222222222223` (`0x3fcfa4fa4fa4fa50`) | Excel 16.0 build 20131, Windows; bitness not recorded, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |
| `DURATION(46356, 46446, 0.05, 0.02, 2, 2)` | settlement `46356` (`0x40e6a28000000000`); maturity `46446` (`0x40e6adc000000000`); rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); yld `0.02` (`0x3f947ae147ae147b`); frequency `2` (`0x4000000000000000`); basis `2` (`0x4000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.2472222222222222` (`0x3fcfa4fa4fa4fa4f`) | Excel 16.0 build 20131, Windows; bitness not recorded, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |

Basis (inferred): All counts are quoted from the DnaCalc commit message and its bead comment
(full bank, per-row traces before and after); the recorded bank rows were not re-read for this
note. The two cited rows are build 20131 readings of a one-coupon bond at two yields, whose
answers differ in the last place.

Inferred, not measured: That Excel stores S(off + n) and then subtracts 1 is inferred from the
match; the bank only shows that this form, with a general loop at one coupon left, reproduces
more rows than each variant tried.

### FN-ECMA.CEILING-001: ECMA.CEILING follows CEILING's sign and zero rules, returning #NUM! for positive number and negative significance

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 build 20527, ECMA.CEILING(number, significance) uses CEILING's sign and zero
rules rather than CEILING.PRECISE's: it returns 0 when number = 0 or significance = 0, returns
#NUM! when number > 0 and significance < 0, and rounds negative numbers up toward zero when
significance > 0 (using the same 15-significant-digit quotient rounding as CEILING). All 2,773

### FN-EFFECT-001: EFFECT switches from x87-spilled binary squaring to the raw x87 power chain at truncated npery = 2^32 - 1

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20228 and 20430, EFFECT(nominal_rate, npery) truncates npery toward zero,
forms base = RN53(RN64(1 + RN53(RN64(nominal_rate / npery)))), and branches at truncated npery
< u32::MAX (4,294,967,295): below u32::MAX it uses LSB-first binary exponentiation with every
multiply and squaring double-rounded on x87, whereas at and above 4,294,967,295 it switches to
the stored-base raw x87 LN/product/EXP power chain before subtracting 1 in x87. All 2,584
full-bank EFFECT rows match.

| `EFFECT(0.05, 4294967295)` | nominal_rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); npery `4294967295.0` (`0x41efffffffe00000`) (cells) | `0.0512712968775475` (`0x3faa403b3ea009a0`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit, workbook compatibility 2; CPU not recorded |

### FN-ENCODEURL-001: ENCODEURL percent-encodes tilde (~) as %7E, leaves only [A-Za-z0-9.-_] unencoded, and returns #VALUE! past 32,767 UTF-16 units

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, ENCODEURL(text) percent-encodes the UTF-8 bytes of text using
uppercase hex for every byte except ASCII letters, ASCII digits, '-', '.', and '_'—notably
encoding '~' as %7E (unlike RFC 3986 unreserved characters) and spaces as %20. Numbers and
logicals coerce to text as '&' does (ENCODEURL(TRUE) -> "TRUE"), and an encoded output
exceeding 32,767 UTF-16 code units returns #VALUE! (LEN(ENCODEURL(REPT(UNICHAR(233),5000))) ->
30000, while 6000 -> #VALUE!). All 3,064 full-bank ENCODEURL rows match.

| `=LEN(ENCODEURL(REPT(UNICHAR(233),5000)))` | as typed | `30000.0` (`0x40dd4c0000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
