### FN-TEXT-002: In TEXT, an @ applied to a number gives the General display, not the full number

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

A format of @ or @! on a number gives what General gives, not the digits of the number.
TEXT(123456789012345,"@") is 1.23457E+14 and TEXT(1234567890.5,"@") is 1234567891. A quoted @
is a literal: TEXT(x,"""@""") is @ for a positive x, and -@ for a negative one, because the
ordinary sign rule applies. In a format with four sections, @ is the text section and numbers
use the others: TEXT(123456789012345,"0;0;0;@") shows all 15 digits, and
TEXT(-123456789012345,"0;0;0;@") shows them with no minus sign, because the second section has
none.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=TEXT(123456789012345,"@")` | as typed | `1.23457E+14` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TEXT(123456789012345,"General")` | as typed | `1.23457E+14` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TEXT(1234567890.5,"@")` | as typed | `1234567891` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-TIME-001: TIME divides total_seconds by 86400 before taking the fractional day, so TIME(25,0,0) differs by 11 ULP from 1/24

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, TIME(hour, minute, second) truncates each argument, checks each
|arg| <= 32767 and total_seconds >= 0 (returning #NUM! for negative total seconds such as
TIME(0,-1,0)), and evaluates frac(total_seconds / 86400). Because 25*3600/86400 = 1 + 1/24
loses 11 bits when the integer day 1 is subtracted, TIME(25,0,0) returns 0.04166666666666674
(0x3fa5555555555560), 11 ULP above 1/24 (0x3fa5555555555555).

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=TIME(25,0,0)` | as typed | `0.04166666666666674` (`0x3fa5555555555560`) | `0.041666666666666664` (`0x3fa5555555555555`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TIME(0,-1,0)` | as typed | `#NUM!` | — | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TIME(1,30,90)` | as typed | `0.06354166666666666` (`0x3fb0444444444444`) | — | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Correct value: Exact rational 1/24 rounded to nearest binary64

Basis (measured): Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in f2_rows (rows 106-108) and matched
across 1,296/1,296 full-bank and 120/120 pinned TIME rows in Excel 16.0.20430.

### FN-TIMEVALUE-001: TIMEVALUE stores the full serial before subtracting the date floor, losing 16 mantissa bits on date-time text

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, TIMEVALUE parses the string as a full Excel serial first and then
subtracts its integer date floor, so a date-qualified timestamp such as "22-Aug-2008 6:35 AM"
loses the 16 low mantissa bits occupied by date serial 39682 and returns 0.2743055555547471
(0x3fd18e38e38e0000), 16,384 ULP below exact (6*60+35)/1440 (0x3fd18e38e38e38e4). On time-only
strings over 24 hours such as "25:30", TIMEVALUE wraps modulo 24 hours to 0.0625.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=TIMEVALUE("22-Aug-2008 6:35 AM")` | as typed | `0.2743055555547471` (`0x3fd18e38e38e0000`) | `0.2743055555555556` (`0x3fd18e38e38e38e4`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TIMEVALUE("25:30")` | as typed | `0.0625` (`0x3fb0000000000000`) | — | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Correct value: Exact rational 395/1440 rounded to nearest binary64

Basis (measured): Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in jnt_dates_random (rows 48-52) and
f2_rows (rows 55-57), and matched across 2,189/2,189 full-bank TIMEVALUE rows.

- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/witness-status.tsv`, TIMEVALUE at `95eb0cb2ef` — 2,189/2,189 full-bank TIMEVALUE rows matched

### FN-TINV-001: TINV for p up to 0.85 is SQRT(v*(1/z - 1)) on a binary64 beta coordinate z, so its last digits follow z

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-11.* Applies to T.INV.2T, TINV.

For df >= 2 and p <= 0.85, the recorded TINV answers lie in the image of the map t = SQRT(v *
(1/z - 1)) over binary64 values z, with v the degrees of freedom and z the inverse of the
regularized beta at (v/2, 1/2). Because z is a double, the t found this way can sit many units
from the true root of the t distribution: TINV(0.85, 25) is 176 units in the last place from
the root's t only through this map. DNA Calc takes, of the two adjacent doubles that bracket
the beta root, the one whose forward value is nearer p. On the full bank this took TINV from 15
to 22 matched of 32 rows (+8 and -1: TINV(0.003, 25) was lost) and its worst miss from 173 to
17 units; the oracle corpus passed count went from 76,765 to 76,769 (CONFIDENCE.T, T.INV.2T and
TINV rows fixed). For p near 1 Excel uses another route: at p = 0.97 three rows are still 10 to
17 units off the t-space bisection DNA Calc keeps there.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TINV(0.85, 25)` | probability `0.85` (`0x3feb333333333333`); deg_freedom `25` (`0x4039000000000000`) (cells) | `0.1910880727923691` (`0x3fc87592efa6421e`) | Excel 16.0 build 20131, Windows; bitness not recorded, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |
| `TINV(0.003, 25)` | probability `0.003` (`0x3f689374bc6a7efa`); deg_freedom `25` (`0x4039000000000000`) (cells) | `3.2870045257248206` (`0x400a4bc9075e5636`) | Excel 16.0 build 20131, Windows; bitness not recorded, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |

Basis (measured): Two Excel build 20131 TINV rows are cited. The mechanism and the counts are
quoted from the DnaCalc commit message and bead comment (harvest 10, R3); the 32-row bank was
not re-read here.

Inferred, not measured: That Excel computes t through z is inferred from the recorded rows
lying in the image of the map; that z is the nearer-to-p bracketing double is DNA Calc's rule,
with 2 of the rows in that image still off because DNA Calc's beta forward value is not
Excel's.

- Open: TINV(0.003, 25) was matched before the change and is lost after it.
- Open: The p = 0.97 route and the TINV p-to-1 behaviour (tracked as dc-6332.13).

Evidence:

- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/src/ported/chi_f_t_family.rs`, t_inv_2t_kernel at `968557b72f` — the route as implemented
- DnaCalc `crates/calc-func/witness-status.tsv`, TINV; BETA.DIST; BETADIST at `968557b72f` — matched rows per function
- DnaCalc `.beads/issues.jsonl`, dc-6332.4 at `b8738ae6a6` — item 3

### FN-TREND-001: TREND evaluates its QR fit and prediction in stored-PC64 x87 arithmetic, drifting by 1-4 ULP on exact lines

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, TREND solves the linear least-squares fit using the same Householder
QR factorization in stored-PC64 x87 arithmetic as LINEST (including unpermuted predictor
ordering and reverse back-substitution) and evaluates predictions with stored-PC64 arithmetic.
Even on the three-point regression y={1;5;3}, x={1;2;3} whose exact least-squares line is x+1,
TREND(..., 0) returns 0.9999999999999996 (4 ULP below 1), TREND(..., 1) returns
1.9999999999999998 (1 ULP below 2), and TREND(..., 100) returns 101.00000000000003 (2 ULP above
101). Paired 2x2 histories are read as four paired observations, where non-numeric scalar new_x
returns #VALUE!.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `=@TREND({1;5;3},{1;2;3},0)` | as typed | `0.9999999999999996` (`0x3feffffffffffffc`) | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=@TREND({1;5;3},{1;2;3},1)` | as typed | `1.9999999999999998` (`0x3fffffffffffffff`) | `2.0` (`0x4000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=@TREND({1;5;3},{1;2;3},100)` | as typed | `101.00000000000003` (`0x4059400000000002`) | `101.0` (`0x4059400000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Correct value: Exact OLS fit to {(1,1),(2,5),(3,3)} is y = x + 1, yielding 1 at x=0
Correct value: Exact OLS fit y = x + 1 at x = 1
Correct value: Exact OLS fit y = x + 1 at x = 100

Basis (measured): Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in dcj9k_regression (rows 22-27) and
dcj9k_r26_regression, and matched across 1,532/1,532 full-bank and 12/12 pinned TREND rows.

### FN-TRIMMEAN-001: TRIMMEAN rejects percent = 1 with #NUM! and sums kept values in original input order rather than sorted order

*Documentation differs from behaviour; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20430 and 16.0.20527, TRIMMEAN(array, percent) rejects percent = 1 with #NUM!
(while accepting percent = 0.9999999999), and sums the untrimmed elements in their original
input order rather than sorted order. On row 1142 of dcj9k_statistics, input-order addition
yields 0x406ba50a3d70a3d8 (221.15750000000003) whereas adding the sorted kept slice gives
0x406ba50a3d70a3d7.

Documentation: Microsoft's TRIMMEAN documentation states that #NUM! is returned only when
percent < 0 or percent > 1.
(https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trimmean-function-d90c9878-a119-4746-88fa-63d988f511d3)

|---|---|---|---|
| `=TRIMMEAN({495.152,175,491.9,354.9,10,130,-73.692,186},0.12)` | as typed | `221.15750000000003` (`0x406ba50a3d70a3d8`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=TRIMMEAN(Data!A1:A3,0.2)` | as typed | `3.0` (`0x4008000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): Measured across 120 TRIMMEAN rows in dcj9k_statistics and prefix_metadata

### FN-TRIMRANGE-001: TRIMRANGE accepts 3 arguments (0 none, 1 leading, 2 trailing, 3 both default), rejects fractional modes with #VALUE!, and returns #REF! on an all-blank input

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to OP_TRIM_REF_BOTH, OP_TRIM_REF_LEADING,
OP_TRIM_REF_TRAILING, TRIMRANGE.

Measured in Excel 16.0.20527 on 26 catalogue calls (sheet dch9u_functions), TRIMRANGE(range,
[trim_rows], [trim_cols]) takes at most three arguments and defaults both trim_rows and
trim_cols to 3 (both margins). Code 0 keeps all margins, 1 trims leading blanks, 2 trims
trailing blanks, and 3 trims both; string "2" coerces to 2 and TRUE coerces to 1, while
non-integer 2.9, out-of-range 4 or -1, and a multi-area union (A1:A3,A5:A9) return #VALUE!. A
completely blank range or array returns #REF! (not #CALC!). TRIMRANGE also accepts array
constants (ROWS(TRIMRANGE({1,2},1)) is 1) and scalar numbers, text, or logicals. The
trim-reference operators save in files as _xlfn._TRO_TRAILING(ref) for A1:.B9 (mode 2),
_xlfn._TRO_LEADING(ref) for A1.:B9 (mode 1), and _xlfn._TRO_ALL(ref) for A1.:.B9 (mode 3), and
evaluate identically to TRIMRANGE with both trim modes equal.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=ROWS(TRIMRANGE(Data!A1:A20,2.9))` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ROWS(TRIMRANGE(Data!F1:F20))` | as typed | `#REF!` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ROWS(TRIMRANGE({1,2},1))` | as typed | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=ROWS(Data!A1.:A20)` | as typed | `20.0` (`0x4034000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): 26 recorded Excel 16.0.20527.20088 readings in catalogue sheet
dch9u_functions (rows 17-38 for TRIMRANGE and rows 39-44 for trim-reference operators) with
Data!A1:A3 holding numbers, Data!A4:A20 blank, and Data!F1:F20 blank.

### FN-TRUE-001: TRUE takes no arguments, refuses any argument at entry, and returns the logical TRUE

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, TRUE() takes zero arguments, rejects any argument or call
postfix at formula entry, and evaluates to the logical value TRUE (distinct from the text
string "TRUE": logical TRUE compares greater than numbers and text, and coerces to 1 only as a
direct argument while being skipped in cell ranges by numeric aggregates).

### FN-TRUNC-001: TRUNC of DBL_MIN returns a subnormal, not 0

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to
ROUNDDOWN, ROUNDUP, TRUNC.

With DBL_MIN (0x0010000000000000) as number, TRUNC, ROUNDDOWN and ROUNDUP return the subnormal
0x000ffffffffffffa at each num_digits recorded, so TRUNC(DBL_MIN,0) is not 0. That value is 6
steps below DBL_MIN and 3 steps below 0x000ffffffffffffd, the binary64 nearest the 15-digit
reading 2.22507385850720E-308. The recorded rows hold 256 such cases for each of the three
functions. ROUND gives 0 on the same inputs.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TRUNC(2.2250738585072014e-308, 0)` | number `2.2250738585072014e-308` (`0x0010000000000000`); num_digits `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `2.2250738585071984e-308` (`0x000ffffffffffffa`) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |
| `TRUNC(2.2250738585072014e-308, 1)` | number `2.2250738585072014e-308` (`0x0010000000000000`); num_digits `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) (cells) | `2.2250738585071984e-308` (`0x000ffffffffffffa`) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |

Correct value: DBL_MIN is below 1, so truncating it at 0 or 1 places gives 0.

Basis (measured): Recorded rows of the broad capture; counts from the rounding write-up.

- Open: Why this one input converts 3 steps below nearest.

Evidence:

### FN-UNIQUE-001: UNIQUE deduplicates text case-insensitively keeping the first spelling, while comparing numbers by binary64 value

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, UNIQUE compares text case-insensitively and retains the first
spelling encountered (CONCAT(UNIQUE({"a";"A";"b"})) returns "ab"), whereas numbers are compared
by exact binary64 value without a tolerance window, so 0.3 and 0.1+0.2 remain distinct
(ROWS(UNIQUE(VSTACK(0.3,0.1+0.2))) returns 2).

### FN-UPPER-001: UPPER applies simple single-codepoint Unicode case mapping without expanding ß/ﬀ or applying Turkish dotted-I rules

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088 and 16.0.19822, UPPER performs single-codepoint BMP case mapping
without full Unicode SpecialCasing expansions or NFC normalization: "straße" becomes "STRAßE"
(not "STRASSE"), "ﬀoo" remains "ﬀOO", "Istanbul" becomes "ISTANBUL" (not Turkish dotted İ),
dotless "ı" becomes "I", Greek final "ς" becomes "Σ", and Deseret U+10428 ("𐐨") above U+FFFF
is unchanged. In compatibility version 1, @UNICHAR(454) returns #NAME? (pre-2013 function
prefix) whereas compatibility version 2 supports it.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=UPPER("hello World")` | as typed | `HELLO WORLD` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=UPPER("a"&LEFT(UNICHAR(128512),1))` | as typed | `A😀` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

Basis (measured): Measured across dcfl2_text (row 46), f2_rows (row 16), jnt_text_formats (rows

### FN-VALUE-001: Text to number reads Arabic, Persian, Devanagari and Thai digits, but not fullwidth digits

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to DATEVALUE, SQRT, VALUE.

In the recorded en-ZA settings, converting text to a number accepts Arabic-Indic (U+0660 to
U+0669), extended Arabic-Indic (U+06F0 to U+06F9), Devanagari (U+0966 to U+096F) and Thai
(U+0E50 to U+0E59) digits. They work alone, in runs, with a decimal point, in the exponent,
with a sign or percent, and mixed with ASCII digits or with each other: VALUE("1٢3") is 123,
and SQRT of a four-digit string using four scripts is the root of 1234. Fullwidth digits
(U+FF10 to U+FF19) give #VALUE! alone or mixed. DATEVALUE reads the four accepted scripts in a
date written year-month-day.

| `=VALUE("๑")` | as typed | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-VALUE-002: A date as text takes at most two digits for month and day

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to DATEVALUE, VALUE.

In a three-part numeric date, leading zeros are not free. VALUE("2024/02/01") is 45323, but
VALUE("2024/02/001") and VALUE("2024/002/01") are #VALUE!, and so is any month or day of three
or more digits in the 45 forms read. A year of one, two or four digits is read: "1/2/1" and
"1/02/01" are 2001-02-01, "24/2/1" is 2024-02-01, while "0001/2/1" is #VALUE!. Month 0 and day
0 give #VALUE!. The same limit holds with hyphens: "2024-02-001" through VALUE, and
"2024-002-01" and "2024-02-001" through DATEVALUE, are #VALUE!. The settings of this run are
en-ZA: decimal point, space as thousands separator, year-month-day date order.

### FN-VALUE-003: VALUE takes one percent sign anywhere around parentheses, and a euro sign but not a dollar

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

VALUE reads parentheses as a negative sign and one percent sign in any of these places: "(1)%",
"(1) %", "(1%)", "(%1)" and "%(1)" are all -0.01. A second percent sign, as in "(1%)%", "%(1)%"
and "(1)%%", gives #VALUE!, as does trailing text. The euro sign is read as a currency sign in
the recorded en-ZA settings: "€1", "1€", "€ 1", "€-1", "-€1", "(€1)" and "€(1)" are 1 or -1.
"$1" and "£1" are #VALUE! there. Currency and percent do not combine: "€1%", "(€1)%" and

### FN-VAR.S-001: The variance family uses raw moments with stored steps, and two tests switch it to a centered sum

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to STDEV,
STDEV.P, STDEV.S, STDEVA, STDEVP, STDEVPA, VAR, VAR.P, VAR.S, VARA, VARP, VARPA.

With RN(v) meaning v rounded to 64 bits on the x87 unit and then stored to binary64, S the
running RN sum of the n values and Q the running RN sum of RN(x*x), the sample variance is
RN(RN(Q - RN(RN(S*S)/n))/(n-1)) and the population variance RN(RN(RN(n*Q) - RN(S*S))/RN(n*n)).
Excel then uses a centered sum instead, adding RN(d*d) with d = RN(x - mean) and dividing by
n-1 or n, when either of two stored tests holds: RN(RN(RN(S*S)/n)/Q) > 0.99, or
RN(variance*1000) <= |RN(S/n)|. The STDEV functions are the root of this, rounded to 64 bits
and then stored. So the answer depends on which path a call takes: the first two VAR.S calls
below differ by a few input steps in two arguments, the first passes the 0.99 test and is
correctly rounded, and the second takes the raw moments and lands 76 units high. The next pair
shows the size test: scaling the inputs by 4 leaves the first path.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Correct value | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `VAR.S(0.8769085090206681, 1, 1.123091490979332)` | number1 `0.8769085090206681` (`0x3fec0fa26efa7e14`); number2 `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); number3 `1.123091490979332` (`0x3ff1f82ec882c0f6`) (cells) | `0.01515151515151495` (`0x3f8f07c1f07c1e94`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows; bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading |
| `VAR.S(0.8769085090206679, 1, 1.1230914909793321)` | number1 `0.8769085090206679` (`0x3fec0fa26efa7e12`); number2 `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); number3 `1.1230914909793321` (`0x3ff1f82ec882c0f7`) (cells) | `0.015151515151515138` (`0x3f8f07c1f07c1f00`) | `0.015151515151515006` (`0x3f8f07c1f07c1eb4`) | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows; bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading |
| `VAR.S(3.244042371786199e-10, 0.00034050419142641947)` | number1 `3.244042371786199e-10` (`0x3df64afacd3a935a`); number2 `0.00034050419142641947` (`0x3f3650b65dc7a1d6`) (cells) | `5.797144172853e-08` (`0x3e6f1f88c6bbc51a`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows; bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading |
| `VAR.S(1.2976169487144796e-09, 0.0013620167657056779)` | number1 `1.2976169487144796e-09` (`0x3e164afacd3a935a`); number2 `0.0013620167657056779` (`0x3f5650b65dc7a1d6`) (cells) | `9.275430676564799e-07` (`0x3eaf1f88c6bbc519`) | `9.2754306765648e-07` (`0x3eaf1f88c6bbc51a`) | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows; bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading |
| `=VAR.S({157,376.82,189.207,12.38,12.473,483,306.24,324.1852,482.235,78})` | as typed | `31907.480453381795` (`0x40df28debfbf8a84`) | `31907.480453381777` (`0x40df28debfbf8a7f`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `STDEV.S(0, 1, 1.031052478719249)` | number1 `0` (`0x0000000000000000`); number2 `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`); number3 `1.031052478719249` (`0x3ff07f30e248f14c`) (cells) | `0.5865198874587454` (`0x3fe2c4c55ae2d85e`) | — | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows; bitness and CPU not recorded in this reading |

Correct value: Exact rational variance of the binary64 inputs, correctly rounded.

Basis (measured): All 14,679 recorded rows of the twelve functions match: VAR.S, VAR.P, VAR,
VARP, VARA, VARPA, STDEV.S, STDEV.P, STDEV, STDEVP, STDEVA and STDEVPA. Six of those rows
separate the stored steps from plain binary64. 910 fresh scalar variance readings (Excel build
20527) replay exactly in rational arithmetic. Four cancellation edges were bisected to adjacent
inputs; sixteen triples chosen to separate the stored ratio from 0.99*Q and from a division by
0.99 all agree with the ratio, where 0.99*Q misses all 16 and the division 14. Seven of eight
magnitude brackets reach adjacent inputs, and sixteen chosen roots all need the 64-bit root
followed by a store.

Inferred, not measured: These tests were located with scalar arguments in separate cells; that
the same edges hold for ranges and arrays is inferred, and their readings have not been taken.
RN(variance*1000) <= |mean| is not separated from the rearrangement variance <= |mean|/1000.
That a raw moment which overflows also takes the centered sum is inferred from recorded answers
that stay finite.

- Open: Whether the two tests keep the same edges for ranges and arrays.

### FN-VDB-001: An empty factor slot in VDB is 0, not the default 2

*Documentation differs from behaviour; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

VDB defaults factor to 2 only when the argument is left off the end of the call. An empty slot,
as in VDB(c,s,l,a,b,,FALSE), is read as 0, and the result is the straight-line amount: 90 here,
where factor 2 gives 160. Text factors other than numbers give #VALUE!, including "TRUE" and
"FALSE", while "2" is read as 2.

Documentation: If factor is omitted, it is assumed to be 2 (the double-declining balance
method).
(https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vdb-function-dde4e207-f3fa-488d-91d2-66d55e861d73)

### FN-WEBSERVICE-001: WEBSERVICE requires _xlfn., caps URLs at 2048 chars, stops https->http redirects, and decodes bodies leniently as UTF-8

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527 (64-bit), _xlfn.WEBSERVICE(url) trims surrounding spaces, rejects non-text,
empty text, URLs > 2048 characters, and schemes other than http/https or host:port with #VALUE!
before issuing any GET request, percent-encodes spaces/%20, #/%23, and non-ASCII path bytes,
follows up to 25 redirects except stopping https-to-http redirects with empty text, caps
responses at 32,767 UTF-16 code units, rejects UTF-16 BOMs (FF FE / FE FF) with #VALUE!, and
decodes bodies leniently as UTF-8 regardless of charset header (so bytes E9 6C 6C decode to
U+9B2C and C0 80 decodes to NUL).

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=_xlfn.WEBSERVICE("http://mock/latin1")` | as typed | `h鬬o` | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |
| `=_xlfn.WEBSERVICE("http://mock/utf16")` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |
| `=_xlfn.WEBSERVICE(123)` | as typed | `#VALUE!` | Excel 16.0 build 20527, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |

Basis (measured): Measured in Excel 16.0.20527 (64-bit) against a local mock server on
2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07 (documented in calc-func/src/fetch.rs and verified by unit/host

- Open: Some raw binary byte bodies (PNG, deflate stream, 00..FF) return #VALUE! in Excel without a published rule yet (fetch.rs lines 34-35).

### FN-WEEKNUM-001: WEEKNUM with an invalid return_type can answer differently each time it is called

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.*

The documentation says an out-of-range return_type gives #NUM!. Excel usually does, but not
always, and the same call can give different answers. In recorded captures of build 20430, 479
(serial_number, return_type) pairs were read with different results: usually #NUM!, sometimes a
number (0, 1, 9, 10, 53 or 54), and some pairs differ within one run file. In build 20527 a
matrix of 1,926 pairs (serial_number 0, 1, 59, 60, 61 and 43831, return_type -32 to 288) was
read twice in one request, and 623 pairs differed between the two readings: 619 between a
number and #NUM!, and 4 between 9 and 10. Every difference has an undocumented return_type. The
ten documented return_types (1, 2, 11 to 17 and 21) gave the same answer both times. No rule
for the undocumented values is claimed.

Documentation: If Return_type is out of the range specified in the table above, a #NUM! error
is returned.
(https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/weeknum-function-e5c43a03-b4ab-426c-b411-b18c13c75340)

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WEEKNUM(0, 23)` | serial_number `0` (`0x0000000000000000`); return_type `23` (`0x4037000000000000`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |
| `WEEKNUM(0, 23)` | serial_number `0` (`0x0000000000000000`); return_type `23` (`0x4037000000000000`) (cells) | `1` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |
| `WEEKNUM(0, 33)` | serial_number `0` (`0x0000000000000000`); return_type `33` (`0x4040800000000000`) (cells) | `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |
| `WEEKNUM(0, 33)` | serial_number `0` (`0x0000000000000000`); return_type `33` (`0x4040800000000000`) (cells) | `#NUM!` | Excel 16.0 build 20430, Windows 64-bit, CPU not recorded in this capture |

Basis (measured): The readings conflict with each other. The 479 comes from the DnaCalc witness
differences file. The 1,926 pairs come from one request of 3,852 calls, with exact input
read-backs, compared pair by pair.

- Open: What decides the answer for an undocumented return_type is not known.
- Open: The raw readings of build 20527 are not yet in a published capture. Their counts are recorded in the DnaCalc issue tracker.

### FN-WEIBULL-001: WEIBULL and WEIBULL.DIST return 0 for PDF at x = 0 and use double-rounded x87 powers diverging up to 4.2 ULP

*Excel differs from the mathematical answer; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to
WEIBULL, WEIBULL.DIST.

In Excel 16.0.20131 and 16.0.20527, WEIBULL and WEIBULL.DIST return 0 at x = 0 even in PDF mode
(cumulative = FALSE) and even when alpha <= 1, after checking that beta^alpha neither overflows
(#NUM!) nor underflows to 0 or a subnormal (#DIV/0!). For x > 0, Excel evaluates r =
RN53(RN64(x/beta)) and raw x87 exp(RN53(RN64(alpha*ln(r)))) powers, returning -expm1(-t) for
CDF or left-to-right double-rounded (alpha/beta^alpha)*x^(alpha-1)*exp(-t) for PDF, differing
up to 4.2 ULP from the true mathematical CDF/PDF. WEIBULL.DIST returns #NAME? in compatibility
version 1.

| `WEIBULL.DIST(6.033375577928498, 2, 2, TRUE)` | x `6.033375570060644` (`0x4018222d34979553`); alpha `2.0` (`0x4000000000000000`); beta `2.0` (`0x4000000000000000`); cumulative `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) (cells) | `0.9998883794284759` (`0x3fefff15ea2976ba`) | `0.999888379428476` (`0x3fefff15ea2976bb`) | Excel 16.0.20131, Windows (bitness not recorded), AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |
| `=@WEIBULL.DIST(105,20,100,TRUE)` | as typed | `#NAME?` | — | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-WORKDAY-001: An empty cell as a first date is serial 0, but a logical in that cell is #VALUE!

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to NETWORKDAYS, NETWORKDAYS.INTL, TBILLEQ,
TBILLPRICE, TBILLYIELD, WORKDAY, WORKDAY.INTL, YEARFRAC.

A reference to an empty cell as the first date of these functions reads as serial 0 and gives a
normal answer: NETWORKDAYS(B1,5) is 4 and WORKDAY(B1,2) is 3. YEARFRAC(B1,5,0) is 5/360. TRUE
in the same cell gives #VALUE!, as a direct TRUE does, so a blank is not treated as the logical

### FN-WRAPCOLS-001: WRAPCOLS and WRAPROWS ignore an error in pad_with when no padding cell is needed and lift over array wrap_count

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to WRAPCOLS, WRAPROWS.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, WRAPCOLS and WRAPROWS require wrap_count >= 1 (0 gives #NUM!) and
only use pad_with for trailing incomplete rows or columns: when no padding is needed, an error
passed in pad_with (such as #VALUE!) is ignored. When wrap_count is an array, Excel lifts the
call over wrap_count's shape.

### FN-XMATCH-001: XMATCH and XLOOKUP equate ligatures and combining sequences in exact mode, while wildcard ? counts UTF-16 units

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to XLOOKUP, XMATCH.

In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, XMATCH and XLOOKUP in default exact mode (match_mode 0) equate text
by Excel's full collation rather than UTF-16 length: "e"&UNICHAR(769) matches precomposed "é",
"ss"/"SS" matches "ß", "ae" matches "æ", and "a"&UNICHAR(173)&"b" matches "ab". By contrast,
wildcard mode (match_mode 2) counts "?" in UTF-16 code units ("??" matches "😀", "?" skips to
"a"). Unlike MATCH/VLOOKUP, blank lookup_value matches blank cells, and approximate searches
order numbers < text < logicals < errors < blanks.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `=XLOOKUP("SS",D5:D16,D5:D16)` | as typed | `ß` | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=XMATCH("ae",D7:D16)` | as typed | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=XMATCH("??",{"😀";"a";"ab"},2)` | as typed | `1.0` (`0x3ff0000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
| `=XMATCH("?",{"😀";"a";"ab"},2)` | as typed | `2.0` (`0x4000000000000000`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |

### FN-XNPV-001: XNPV rejects rate <= 0 with #NUM!, rejects non-numeric cells in vectors, and uses worksheet POWER

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20131 and 16.0.20527, XNPV(rate, values, dates) returns #NUM! for rate <= 0
(including rate = 0 and -0.0) while accepting +1e-300, rejects text, logicals, and blank cells
inside values or dates with #VALUE!, rejects 2-D arrays with #REF!, truncates dates, and
requires all dates >= dates[0]. It evaluates years = (date - anchor) / 365 in binary64, base =

### FN-YEARFRAC-001: On basis 1 the fictitious 1900-02-29 is not a leap day, and YEARFRAC takes serial 0 as a date

*Quirk; measured; recorded 2026-11-04.* Applies to ACCRINTM, DISC, INTRATE, PRICEDISC,
RECEIVED, YEARFRAC.

Excel's calendar holds a 29 February 1900, serial 60, that never existed. On basis 1
(actual/actual) it does not make 1900 a leap year: YEARFRAC(59,60,1) is 1/365, where the real
1904-02-29 gives YEARFRAC(1520,1521,1) = 1/366. Serial 0 is accepted as a date: YEARFRAC(0,5,0)
is 5/360 and YEARFRAC(0,60,1) is 60/365. Reversed dates give the same answer as in order.
ACCRINTM, DISC, INTRATE, PRICEDISC and RECEIVED take the same 365 and 366 on those dates:
DISC(59,60,99,100,1) is about 3.65 and DISC(1520,1521,99,100,1) about 3.66.

### FN-YIELD-001: YIELD near par on a coupon date returns a closed-form seed with stored partial sums, not the solved root

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-11.*

On a coupon date, with redemption 100 and more than one coupon period left, YIELD at a price
close to 100 does not return the root of the price equation. It returns the closed-form seed y
= f * ((n*cp - d) / (d*(n+1)/2 + n*R)), with n the periods left, cp = 100*rate/f the coupon per
period, R the redemption and d = price - R, whenever the Newton step (P(y) - price) / P'(y)
taken at the seed is below 1e-10; otherwise the solver runs. On the recorded 20228 and 20527
rows Excel's switch lies between steps of 8.8e-11 and 1.17e-10. The association of the seed
matters: DNA Calc forms the total coupon as S(S(S(n*rate)*100)/f) and the denominator as
S(S(n*R + S(S(d*n)/2)) + S(d/2)), each partial result stored to binary64 before the next, and
with that association 31 more full-bank rows matched (YIELD 66 to 97 of 533, none lost). The
same seed is taken at a price of exactly 100: Excel does not return the coupon rate directly
there, so DNA Calc's former shortcut for price 100 and redemption 100 was removed. Before the
seed was introduced (commit d44aaf0a) YIELD matched 16 of 533 bank rows with a worst miss of
4.4e15 units in the last place; with the plain binary64 seed it matched 66 with a worst miss of
2,844 units. Offline, that plain binary64 order reproduced Excel's bits on 64 of the 97
small-step rows with redemption 100, against at most 58 for the x87-extended orders tried.

| Call | Inputs (binary64) | Excel | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `YIELD(44013, 44562, 0.05, 100.00001525878906, 100, 2, 0)` | settlement `44013` (`0x40e57da000000000`); maturity `44562` (`0x40e5c24000000000`); rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); pr `100.00001525878906` (`0x4059000040000000`); redemption `100` (`0x4059000000000000`); frequency `2` (`0x4000000000000000`); basis `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.04999989318848743` (`0x3fa9999604189993`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |
| `YIELD(44013, 46753, 0.05, 99.99999713897711, 100, 2, 0)` | settlement `44013` (`0x40e57da000000000`); maturity `46753` (`0x40e6d42000000000`); rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); pr `99.99999713897711` (`0x4058fffff4000004`); redemption `100` (`0x4059000000000000`); frequency `2` (`0x4000000000000000`); basis `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.050000004577636696` (`0x3fa99999c0ebedf7`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |
| `YIELD(44013, 46753, 0.05, 100.000002861023, 100, 2, 0)` | settlement `44013` (`0x40e57da000000000`); maturity `46753` (`0x40e6d42000000000`); rate `0.05` (`0x3fa999999999999a`); pr `100.000002861023` (`0x405900000c000004`); redemption `100` (`0x4059000000000000`); frequency `2` (`0x4000000000000000`); basis `0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.04999999542236326` (`0x3fa9999972474536`) | Excel 16.0 build 20228, Windows 64-bit; CPU not recorded |

Basis (measured): Three recorded rows are cited (Excel build 20228, near-seed discovery set);
the unit test in DnaCalc holds five rows (three from 20228 and two price 100 + 1 ulp rows at a
zero coupon from build 20527) and DNA Calc returns Excel's recorded bits on all five. The
matched counts are quoted from the commit messages (full bank, per-row traces).

Inferred, not measured: That Excel's code forms this seed, with this association and this 1e-10
switch, is inferred; the seed form is read off the bank, and the switch only brackets between
8.8e-11 and 1.17e-10.

- Open: Rows 024 and 026 of the bank (basis-dependent) stay unmatched.
- Open: Designs with redemption other than 100 (the oncoupon-b4-f1 rows: step below 1e-10 at the seed but Excel about 450 units from it) carry a seed that is not identified.
- Open: 26 rows of the oncoupon-short design are one unit below Excel: the evaluation order of the seed is open there.

### FN-YIELD-002: Multi-period YIELD starts from a schedule-free par-100 seed, steps analytic Newton on 1+y/f, and publishes pre-step y when |step| <= 1e-10

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; inferred; recorded 2026-11-22.*

Superseding the near-par special case in FN-YIELD-001, Excel 16.0.20527 runs one universal
solver for all multi-period YIELD calls (n > 1), regardless of coupon date or redemption. It
first computes a schedule-free years-to-maturity T (using US/European 30/360 / 360 for bases 0
and 4, and k + (m - s_k) / year_days for bases 1..3 where s_k uses DATE(sy + k, sm, sd) day
rollover), forms d = price - 100.0 (hardcoded 100.0, never redemption), and sets the initial
iterate y_0 = f * ((tau * rate * 100 / f - d) / ((tau * 100 + d * tau / 2) + d * f / 4)). Each
Newton step evaluates base = 1.0 + y / f (whose rounding into [1, 2) produces +109-ULP sawtooth
jumps as y crosses base binade boundaries), sums coupon and redemption terms using
excel_bond_pow, and checks |step| <= 1e-10 (0x3ddb7cdfd9d7bdbb): when satisfied, Excel returns
the un-updated iterate y before subtracting step (leaving up to 2,844 ULP differences when
|step_0| <= 1e-10). After 100 iterations without stopping, Excel returns y_100.

| `YIELD(44256, 46753, 0.09, 117.26480472366886, 105, 4, 0)` | settlement `44242.0` (`0x40e59a4000000000`); maturity `45658.0` (`0x40e64b4000000000`); rate `0.0875` (`0x3fb6666666666666`); pr `117.26480472366886` (`0x405d50f28f82fefb`); redemption `105.0` (`0x405a400000000000`); frequency `4.0` (`0x4010000000000000`); basis `0.0` (`0x0000000000000000`) (cells) | `0.049999999999982156` (`0x3fa9999999998f8e`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20196, Windows 64-bit, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H with Radeon Graphics |

Basis (inferred): Measured across 3,198 cb4 live Excel 16.0.20527 calls and two prospective

witness bank from 3,053 to 3,489 of 3,489 (+436, worst ULP 2,844 -> 0) and the pinned bank from

Inferred, not measured: The exact Newton loop form and 100-iteration fallback are inferred from

### FN-YIELDDISC-001: YIELDDISC checks basis before required slots, accepts serial 0, and groups B / DIM separately in x87

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20527, YIELDDISC(settlement, maturity, pr, redemption, [basis]) validates the
optional basis (0..=4) before reading settlement, maturity, pr, or redemption, accepts serial 0
and spans crossing the fictitious 1900-02-29 (matching INTRATE day counts), and evaluates
RN53(RN64(RN53(RN64(RN53(RN64(redemption - pr)) / pr)) * RN53(RN64(B / DIM)))) rather than
left-to-right division. All 4,340 full-bank YIELDDISC rows match.

### FN-YIELDMAT-001: YIELDMAT groups ((1 + DIM/B*rate) - term2) / term2 * (B / DSM) with every step stored from x87 PC64

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.*

In Excel 16.0.20131 and 16.0.20527, YIELDMAT(settlement, maturity, issue, rate, pr, [basis])
evaluates term2 = pr/100 + (A/B)*rate, term1 = (1 + (DIM/B)*rate) - term2, and (term1 / term2)
* (B / (DIM - A)) with every arithmetic operation double-rounded from x87 PC64 to binary64. The
left-to-right F# regrouping dim/b*rate + 1 - pr/100 - a/b*rate differs by 1 to 2 ULP. All 1,085
full-bank and 120 pinned YIELDMAT rows match.

### FN-Z.TEST-001: Z.TEST and ZTEST check sample size even with sigma supplied and evaluate NORMSDIST((x - mean) * sqrt(n) / sigma)

*Detail for matching Excel's bits; measured; recorded 2026-11-22.* Applies to Z.TEST, ZTEST.

In Excel 16.0 builds 20326 and 20527, Z.TEST(array, x, [sigma]) requires the _xlfn. prefix in
OOXML (bare @Z.TEST returns #NAME?) while compatibility ZTEST takes no prefix. Both validate
sample length even when sigma is provided (0 values -> #N/A, 1 value -> #DIV/0!), use sample
STDEV.S when sigma is omitted, and compute NORMSDIST((x - mean) * sqrt(n) / sigma); grouping as
(x - mean) / (sigma / sqrt(n)) or 1 - NORMSDIST((mean - x)/se) differs by 1 ULP. Matches
2,857/2,857 Z.TEST and 2,864/2,864 ZTEST full-bank rows.

| `=ZTEST(Data!A1:A3,2)` | as typed | `0.1932381153856163` (`0x3fc8bc06ccf600b4`) | Excel 16.0.20527.20088 Current Channel, Windows 64-bit (NT 10.0.26200), x86-64, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, en-ZA |
